items.title: Chamber inaugurates councils to boost private-sector growth

original_payload.original_title: Chamber inaugurates councils to boost private-sector growth
original_payload.original_body:
Economy/Business  Chamber inaugurates councils to boost private-sector growth
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   10 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Vivian Emoni
The Abuja Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) has inaugurated governing councils for five centres of excellence to strengthen private-sector development and institutional governance.
The ACCI President, Chief Emeka Obegolu, inaugurated the councils on Friday in Abuja, charging members to prioritise accountability, innovation and effective service delivery.
Obegolu said the inauguration formed part of efforts to enhance entrepreneurship, trade facilitation, commercial dispute resolution and sustainable economic development.
“The five centres of excellence are critical pillars of the chamber’s institutional framework and operational structures.
“Their effectiveness will determine the chamber’s capacity to deliver value to members and the wider business community,” he said.
Obegolu said the centres were instrumental in translating the chamber’s strategic objectives and members’ expectations into practical programmes and measurable outcomes.
He urged the newly appointed chairmen and members to demonstrate professionalism, innovation, commitment and accountability in discharging their responsibilities.
The president also encouraged them to consolidate existing achievements, introduce fresh initiatives and deliver tangible results ahead of the chamber’s anniversary celebrations.
He charged programme officers and administrative personnel to facilitate communication, coordinate activities, document decisions and monitor the implementation of work plans.
Obegolu urged the officers to work closely with their respective chairmen to ensure the successful implementation of programmes and initiatives.
Responding on behalf of the councils, Prince Adetokunbo Kayode, Chairman, National Policy Advocacy Centre (NPAC), appreciated the chamber’s leadership for the confidence reposed in them.
Kayode described the appointments as an honour and significant responsibility, pledging collective efforts to advance the centres’ mandates.
He said the centres were established to address critical areas of private-sector development and strengthen the chamber’s national and international relevance.
Kayode pledged that each centre would develop annual strategic and operational work plans to guide activities and establish measurable targets.
He said the new leadership would consolidate existing achievements rather than reinvent established structures, while identifying areas requiring improvement.
Kayode expressed confidence that the centres would commence programmes promptly and collaborate with the chamber’s leadership to achieve meaningful results.
In his remarks, ACCI Second Deputy President, Dr Aliyu Hong, described the inauguration as an important milestone in the chamber’s institutional growth.
Hong commended the chamber’s achievements in organisational development, innovation and the establishment of specialised centres of excellence.
He described the centres as strategic platforms for enterprise development, policy engagement, commercial dispute resolution, trade facilitation and cooperative advancement.
Hong also highlighted the chamber’s growing relevance in international business engagements, citing his participation in a Malaysian business roundtable on Thursday.
He expressed confidence that the experience and expertise of the newly inaugurated governing councils would improve the centres’ performance.
The centres include the Business Entrepreneurship Skills and Technology Centre, National Policy Advocacy Centre and Nigerian Chambers of Commerce Dispute Resolution Centre.
Others are the Abuja Trade Centre and ACCI Multipurpose Cooperative Society. (NAN)
VOE/KTO
=========

items.title: ECOWAS Parliament seeks stronger institutional collaboration to deepen integration

original_payload.original_title: ECOWAS Parliament seeks stronger institutional collaboration to deepen integration
original_payload.original_body:
Foreign  ECOWAS Parliament seeks stronger institutional collaboration to deepen integration
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   15 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Sarafina Christopher
The ECOWAS Parliament has called for stronger institutional collaboration, effective parliamentary oversight and accountability to address West Africa’s security, economic and governance challenges and advance regional integration.
The Speaker of the Parliament, Hajia Memounatu Ibrahima, made the call at the opening of the Parliament’s 2026 Second Ordinary Session on Friday in Abuja.
Ibrahima said the growing complexity of regional challenges required closer cooperation among ECOWAS institutions, stressing that no single institution could address them independently.
She said the Parliament must move beyond observing regional developments to becoming a stronger voice for citizens through enhanced legislative and oversight functions.
The Speaker cited the Lungi Declaration, which reaffirmed ECOWAS leaders’ commitment to strengthening the Parliament’s legislative and oversight responsibilities.
She said sustainable regional integration depended on credible institutions, public trust, democracy, justice and respect for the rule of law.
Ibrahima identified consideration of the proposed 2027 Community Budget as a major priority amid growing financial pressures and development needs across the region.
She urged lawmakers to ensure that budgetary allocations reflected clear priorities, measurable outcomes and tangible benefits for citizens.
She also urged national parliaments to intensify advocacy with their governments to ensure regular collection and remittance of the ECOWAS Community Levy.
According to her, resources entrusted to ECOWAS institutions represented both the contributions and expectations of West African citizens.
Ibrahima commended Cape Verde for its peaceful electoral process and congratulated President José Maria Neves on his re-election.
She expressed hope that forthcoming elections in The Gambia and Nigeria would further strengthen democracy, peace and regional stability.
The President of the ECOWAS Commission, retired Gen. Birame Diop, called for renewed regional solidarity and stronger parliamentary diplomacy to address emerging challenges.
Diop said geopolitical rivalries, economic uncertainties, security threats and competing development priorities had exposed the limitations of individual national responses.
He identified terrorism and insecurity in the Sahel, as well as their spillover effects on coastal countries, as major threats requiring coordinated regional action.
He also advocated renewed engagement with international partners, particularly the United States, to strengthen security cooperation and border safety.
Such partnerships, he said, should promote regional stability and facilitate the free movement of people across West Africa.
Diop noted that the region’s population of more than 400 million, abundant natural resources and entrepreneurial potential offered significant opportunities for economic transformation.
He, however, said these opportunities could only be fully realised through interconnected markets and the removal of trade barriers.
He said ECOWAS was prioritising trade liberalisation, the removal of tariff and non-tariff barriers, improved customs procedures, digitalisation and industrialisation.
Other priorities included developing regional value chains to boost production, competitiveness and economic cooperation among member states.
Diop stressed that regional integration must deliver practical benefits to traders, farmers, entrepreneurs, young people and other citizens.
He described the ECOWAS Parliament as a critical link between regional institutions and citizens, urging stronger legislative and oversight functions.
He said the proposed ECOWAS Agenda 2050 required collective commitment and coordinated action by all Community institutions.
He urged lawmakers to support regional efforts in peace and security, economic and monetary integration, sustainable development and human capital development.
He also identified gender inclusion and digital transformation as essential to the region’s long-term development.
The President of the ECOWAS Court of Justice, Justice Charlyne Brumskine, called for stronger collaboration between the judiciary and Parliament to improve compliance with the Court’s judgments.
Brumskine said both institutions had complementary roles in advancing regional integration and protecting the rights of West African citizens.
She said while Parliament provided citizens with representation and a political voice, the Court offered legal protection and remedies for rights violations.
The Court president said its credibility depended largely on the enforcement of its judgments by member states.
She urged lawmakers to encourage governments to comply with the Court’s decisions and domesticate Community legal instruments to improve access to justice.
Brumskine also highlighted the Court’s Justice 2030 strategic roadmap, which aims to bring the institution closer to citizens, particularly women.
She called for adequate and predictable funding, qualified personnel and modern infrastructure to strengthen the Court’s operations.
She proposed regular institutional dialogue, periodic briefings on judicial activities and jurisprudence, and stronger parliamentary support for enforcing the Court’s judgments.
Brumskine reaffirmed the Court’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with Parliament and other ECOWAS institutions.
NAN reports that the two-week session will feature the presentation of the Commission president’s strategic plan and the Report on the State of the Community.
Lawmakers will also consider country reports, parliamentary oversight reports and the proposed 2027 Community Budget.
Other issues scheduled for consideration include regional trade facilitation, the ECOWAS Mission in The Gambia and agricultural development projects.
Efforts to strengthen the regional electricity market will also feature during the session.   (NAN)
Edited by Mark Longyen

original_payload.original_title: APC ​‌‌​‌⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍‍‍‌​‌‌​chieftain launches free medical outreach for 30,000 Osun residents
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  APC ​‌‌​‌⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍‍‍‌​‌‌​chieftain launches free medical outreach for 30,000 Osun residents
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   20 minutes ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Moromoke Akanji
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun, Dotun Babayemi, has launched a free medical outreach targeting 30,000 vulnerable residents across the state.
Babayemi, at the flag-off on Friday in Iwo, said 20,000 free eyeglasses would be distributed to beneficiaries through his foundation, the ODB Foundation.
The APC chieftain said the programme was conceived as a way of expressing gratitude to God through service to humanity in celebration of his 60th birthday.
“Instead of throwing any birthday bash, to me, reaching the people in this format is one of my surest ways of thanking God.
“This is because there are many of our people out there who are not aware of their health conditions,” he said.
According to him, the ODB Foundation was designed to extend beyond healthcare and medical interventions to include education and youth empowerment, with the aim of creating a broader platform for sustainable community development.
Babayemi also emphasised the non-partisan nature of the initiative, stressing that the medical outreach was neither a party affair nor politically motivated.
“This is not a party affair, and it is not politically inclined. This initiative is for everybody. Our concern is the health and welfare of the people, irrespective of their political affiliations,” he said.
He added that the medical outreach represented the first phase of the foundation’s activities, noting that plans were underway to empower at least 60 youths across the state to sustain their respective trades and entrepreneurial ventures.
Also, Chairperson of the ODB Foundation, Dr Veronica Babayemi, said the Alafia Dòtun Medical Outreach, which had been organised annually for the past 15 years, had now evolved into the ODB Foundation.
She described the transition as a deliberate step towards institutionalising the humanitarian initiative and creating a sustainable structure capable of attracting broader participation and support.
Babayemi, the wife of the organiser, said the Iwo medical outreach represented the foundation’s first official outing.
According to her,  the vision is to build an enduring institution capable of delivering interventions across multiple areas of human development.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that religious and community leaders, as well as members and chieftains of various political parties attended the event. (NAN)
MAK/VE/AYO
Edited by Victor Adeoti/Ayodeji Alabi

items.title: From Access to Opportunity: India’s decade long journey of transformation

original_payload.original_title: From Access to Opportunity: India’s decade long journey of transformation
original_payload.original_body:
General News  From Access to Opportunity: India’s decade long journey of transformation
By  Ismail Abdulaziz   ·   23 minutes ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Abhishek Singh
The truest test of economic growth is what changes inside a home: whether there is water in the tap, food on the table, a bank account in a mother’s name and a fair chance for her children.
By that test, India’s journey over the past decade emerges as an unprecedented one.
Over the past decade, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s clarion call of   Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas  —Together with All, Development for All, Trust of All, and Efforts of All has served as the guiding philosophy behind India’s socio-economic transformation.
Welfare was looked at from a lens of empowerment, empowering and enabling every citizen to become an active partner in the nation’s progress.
The World Bank’s October 2026 Poverty & Equity Brief highlights one of the fastest sustained declines in poverty anywhere in the world.
Between 2011 and 2023, extreme poverty in India—measured at US$3 a day—fell from 27.1 per cent to 2.6 per cent, while at the higher lower-middle-income line of US$4.20 a day, the poverty rate dropped from 57.7 per cent to 16.1 per cent, lifting roughly 496 million people above the threshold.
These income gains are mirrored by sweeping improvements in human development: multidimensional poverty—which captures overlapping deprivations in health, education, and basic living standards—declined from 29.17 per cent in 2013–14 to 11.28 per cent in 2022–23, moving about 248 million people out of deprivation.
Essentials that restore dignity:
Poverty is not merely having a low income. It is the hours spent fetching water, the smoke in the kitchen and the illness that wipes out a family’s savings.
India has chosen to tackle these deprivations together, with the aim of reaching every eligible household.
Rural homes with tap water rose from 32.3 million in August 2019 to 158.4 million, about 82 per cent, by May 2026.
Under the Swachh Bharat (Clean India) Mission, more than 121 million household toilets have been built.
Over 105 million free cooking-gas connections have gone to women from poor households.
More than 30 million rural and 9.8 million urban homes have been completed under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana housing programme.
Average rural power supply rose from 12.5 hours a day in 2014 to 22.6 hours in 2025.
Security matters as much as access. Free foodgrain reaches to over 810 million people. Ayushman Bharat offers eligible families hospital cover of up to ₹500,000 a year.
Maternal mortality fell from 130 per 100,000 live births in 2014–16 to 88 in 2021–23, while child stunting declined from 38.4 per cent in 2015–16 to 29.3 per cent in 2023–24.
Social protection coverage has expanded from 19 per cent of the population in 2015 to 68.4 per cent in 2026 reaching nearly a billion people.
Delivery that reaches the last citizen:
A programme is only as good as its delivery. Effective delivery through the JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar digital identity and Mobile penetration) has powered what the World Bank’s October 2026 Poverty & Equity Brief highlights as a historic decline in poverty.
Between 2011 and 2023,   496 million Indians   moved out of poverty as rates at the $4.20/day threshold fell from   57.7% to 16.1%  , while extreme poverty ($3.00/day) dropped from   27.1% to 2.6%  .
Growth has been further anchored by expanded social transfers, rising household consumption, and rural women’s employment, supported by scale infrastructure including over   580 million Jan Dhan accounts  ,   ₹6.83 trillion   in direct benefit transfers for FY 2024–25, and high-volume UPI and ration portability systems.
From collective action to opportunity:
Governments can build toilets and lay pipes, but communities make the change last. Sanitation became a people’s movement. Village assemblies certify when their villages achieve full tap-water coverage, and local women have been trained to test water quality.
Women’s self-help groups show this collective strength most vividly. Around 100 million rural women belong to more than nine million groups through which they save, borrow and build enterprises.
By May 2026, over 30 million had become   Lakhpati Didis  , (Millionaire Sisters) women whose annual household income exceeds ₹100,000.
Collateral-free loans have also opened formal credit to small entrepreneurs, with about two-thirds of loans going to women.
These grassroots gains form the bedrock of broader economic growth.
Healthier families, connected villages, and financially included women are better equipped to work, learn, and invest, while rural roads link farmers to markets and children to schools.
According to the World Bank’s October 2026 brief, India added 134 million jobs between 2017 and 2023 nearly double the growth of the working-age population, propelled largely by rural women entering paid work alongside strong consumption growth and expanded social transfers.
It must be acknowledged though that our work is far from finished.
Poverty that remains is increasingly concentrated in particular regions, and many workers need more productive and better-paid jobs.
Meeting these challenges is central to our goal of a developed India, i.e.   Viksit Bharat  , by 2047.
A partnership for shared progress:
India and Nigeria are large, young and diverse democracies with longstanding bilateral ties.
India opened its liaison office in Lagos in 1958, two years before Nigeria’s independence, and our ties became a Strategic Partnership in 2007.
Today, bilateral trade stands at   around   US$   08   billion (April – September 2026), more than 200 Indian companies operate in Nigeria, being the second largest employers of the Nigerian workforce after the Federal Government.
Every nation must chart its own path, and India offers its experience in that spirit.
Our journey shows that basic services are investments in human potential, that digital public infrastructure can narrow the distance between citizen and state, and that development moves faster when women and communities lead it.
India is partnering closely with Nigeria to deepen cooperation in digital public infrastructure, affordable medicines, agriculture, food security, defence, trade and capacity building.
True South–South cooperation demands more than economic statistics; it requires shared growth that reaches every doorstep and transforms the lives of every family.
Singh is the High Commissioner of India to Nigeria,Benin
and the ECOWAS.

items.title: NAF harps on physical fitness for operational effectiveness

original_payload.original_title: NAF harps on physical fitness for operational effectiveness
original_payload.original_body:
Defence/Security  NAF harps on physical fitness for operational effectiveness
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   22 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Lengnan Tobias
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has emphasised the need for structured physical fitness management to enhance personnel welfare and operational effectiveness.
The Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, said physical fitness was not merely a recreation or lifestyle choice, but an essential component of military professionalism
Aneke represented by the Director of Administration, Defence Headquarters, Air Commodore Sunday Bello, said this on Friday in Abuja at the 2nd edition of the Directorate of Sports and Physical Education Workshop 2026,
He said the theme of the workshop, “Optimising Contemporary Physical Fitness Management Activities to Enhance Air Force Transformation”, was timely and relevant in view of the complex and uncertain security environment.
According to him, successful execution of constitutional responsibilities requires personnel who are physically fit, mentally alert, psychologically resilient and capable of optimal performance under pressure.
“The modern battlefield may be shaped by advanced platforms, technology and intelligence capabilities. However, the human element remains central to the effective employment of these capabilities.”
He said fitness management must be approached as a deliberate institutional responsibility, requiring structured programmes, appropriate standards, professional supervision and sustained investment.
He also said that the workshop would provide an opportunity to assess existing practices, identify gaps and explore contemporary approaches to improve physical fitness management in the NAF.
The CAS further said that the workshop aligned with his command philosophy of transforming the NAF into an agile, resilient force that effectively meets airpower demands of national security.
He stressed that personnel welfare and operational effectiveness were mutually reinforcing, noting that a fit workforce was better positioned to withstand operational stress and sustain mission performance.
He however, said fitness activities must be safe, inclusive, professionally guided and supported by medical oversight to minimise preventable injuries.
Aneke urged participants to actively engage resource persons, adding that the success of the workshop should be measured by implementation of its recommendations.
He directed the directorate of sports and physical education to ensure that recommendations translated into practical policies and programmes.
Earlier, the Director of Sports, Air Commodore Samuel Osoniyi, said the workshop was designed to review physical training structures and align them with modern techniques and best practices in sports administration, injury prevention and talent development.
Osoniyi said the forum would also help build a stronger sporting culture across NAF formations and improve performance in local and international competitions.
He thanked the CAS for his support for sports development and commended the organising committee for the programme.(NAN)
Edited by Deborah Coker

items.title: Can new digital payments open West African markets to Nigerian SMEs?

original_payload.original_title: Can new digital payments open West African markets to Nigerian SMEs?
original_payload.original_body:
Features  Can new digital payments open West African markets to Nigerian SMEs?
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   25 minutes ago   ·  8 min read
✓
✓
Can new digital payments open West African markets to Nigerian SMEs?
By Usman Aliyu, News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
Before sunrise at the Nigeria–Benin border in Seme-Krake, Bridget Okafor counts her naira and West African CFA francs, slipping both bundles into a pouch beneath her wrapper.
For eight years, she has supplied cassava flour and dried hibiscus to buyers in Cotonou and Accra.
Yet every journey across the coastal corridor remains a financial obstacle course.
To pay suppliers and receive customers’ payments, Okafor relies on roadside currency changers, informal brokers or bank transfers routed through correspondent banks in New York and London.
Transfers can take seven business days and consume seven per cent to 12 per cent of her profit margin.
“My buyers in Ghana want to pay in cedis, my suppliers in Benin want CFA, and my bank in Nigeria tells me to find dollars first.
“By the time the money settles, the exchange rate has moved and half my profit is gone,” she said.
Central banks, multilateral institutions and fintech companies have invested in instant, local-currency payment infrastructure to connect fragmented markets and support trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).
At the centre is the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), backed by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), alongside regional payment networks and fintech platforms.
Afreximbank estimates the systems could save African businesses more than five billion dollars annually in currency-conversion and correspondent-banking costs.
Yet regulatory fragmentation, foreign-exchange constraints, uneven digital infrastructure and limited awareness continue to exclude many micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).
Because many African currencies are not directly convertible, a Nigerian importer buying from Ghana may convert naira into dollars, route the funds through a correspondent bank in the United States or Europe, and have the receiving bank convert them into cedis.
The double conversion raises costs and exposes businesses to exchange-rate volatility.
Commercially unveiled in Accra in January 2022, PAPSS was designed to reduce this dependence on intermediary currencies.
It connects central banks and commercial financial institutions, allowing a Nigerian business to pay in naira while a supplier in Ghana receives cedis. Participating institutions subsequently settle their net positions.
“We are not chasing de-dollarisation because Africa still needs to trade with the rest of the world. But when Africa trades with itself, let us use PAPSS to reduce the amount of foreign currencies required.
“When a trader in Lagos has to buy dollars just to pay a weaver in Accra, we are subsidising foreign clearing houses and starving our own central banks of reserves.
“Local-currency settlement isn’t just a technical upgrade — it is economic sovereignty,” said Mike Ogbalu, Chief Executive Officer of PAPSS.
More than 22 Nigerian commercial banks, including First Bank, Access Bank, UBA, Sterling Bank, and Wema Bank, have integrated PAPSS across their branches and digital channels.
To boost small-scale cross-border trade, CBN guidelines allow Nigerian SMEs to make eligible monthly payments of up to 5,000 dollars, while individuals can transact up to 2,000 dollars.
Adoption among ordinary traders, however, remains uneven, particularly along the Nigeria-Benin corridor.
A major obstacle is West Africa’s fragmented monetary and regulatory architecture.
Nigeria and Ghana are among the early PAPSS participants through the West African Monetary Zone (WAMZ) framework.
Benin, however, belongs to the eight-country West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU), which uses the CFA franc, pegged to the euro and managed under the regional monetary framework of the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO).
Differences in regulatory approvals, anti-money-laundering rules, foreign-exchange arrangements and settlement procedures complicate efforts to connect the zones.
At Lagos’s Mile 12 International Market, many traders remain unfamiliar with PAPSS.
Chinedu Eze, an importer of woven fabrics and cosmetics from Benin and Ghana, shared his experience.
“If I walk into my bank branch and ask to pay a supplier in Cotonou in naira, half the tellers look at me like I am speaking French.
“Even when the app works for Ghana, my supplier in Benin wants mobile money or cash CFA. If the system doesn’t connect directly to the phone in his pocket, it doesn’t solve my problem,” he said.
The AfricaNenda Foundation’s State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) in Africa Report 2026 identifies 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, but only 16 support cross-border transactions.
The World Bank’s Global Findex 2025 puts the share of African adults without a formal bank account or mobile-money wallet at about 42 per cent.
Nigeria’s payment ecosystem is largely bank-account driven through the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) Instant Payment infrastructure. In Ghana and Benin, mobile-money services such as MTN MoMo, Telecel Cash and Moov Money are widely used.
A Nigerian SME using a banking app to pay a supplier in Kumasi or Porto-Novo who relies on mobile money needs affordable, direct wallet transfers with transparent fees and clear dispute resolution.
This gap hits women hardest, as they make up 60 per cent to 70 per cent of West Africa’s informal cross-border traders. Without reliable digital payments, many are forced to carry cash across borders, exposing them to theft, unfair exchange rates, and extortion.
Funmilayo Adeyemi, founder of a 14-person skincare and shea-butter export business in Ibadan, began supplying boutique retailers in Accra in 2024.
Her Ghanaian customers initially used informal agents, who charged up to nine per cent and sometimes delayed remittances for days.
“When you are a small business, a five-day settlement delay freezes your entire working capital.
“I couldn’t buy raw shea nuts from women cooperatives in Kwara State until my Accra invoice cleared,” she said.
In 2025, Adeyemi adopted a Nigerian cross-border fintech platform alongside a PAPSS-enabled corporate account with her bank. She said settlement time fell from five days to less than an hour, while transaction costs dropped by more than half.
She still faces difficulties with smaller Ghanaian boutiques that lack registered corporate bank accounts or struggle to meet Know-Your-Customer (KYC) requirements.
Lagos fintech executives argue that technology companies can help bridge gaps left by conventional banks.
Platforms such as Flutterwave, Paystack, Leatherback and Klasha have developed payment infrastructure that enables merchants to collect payments in foreign currencies, including cedis and CFA francs, with settlement options varying by market and service.
Some fintechs have experimented with dollar-pegged stablecoins to navigate illiquid foreign-exchange corridors, attracting regulatory scrutiny over capital flight and monetary stability.
Ibrahim Bakare, Chief Operating Officer of Lagos-based cross-border payment startup HAQ Technology Management Services, says closer collaboration between fintechs and banks is essential.
“Fintechs have the user experience and the merchant relationships, while banks hold the central-bank settlement licences and PAPSS direct-participant status.
“When regulators allow fintechs to plug directly into PAPSS as indirect participants rather than forcing us to negotiate slow bilateral deals with multiple banks, costs for SMEs drop overnight,” he said.
Bankers caution that technology cannot resolve foreign-exchange liquidity constraints on its own.
Under PAPSS arrangements, participating financial institutions must maintain adequate settlement liquidity to support transactions. Trade imbalances also require banks and central banks to manage net settlement positions.
“Instant messaging does not magically create foreign-exchange liquidity out of thin air.
“What PAPSS does brilliantly is net off offsetting trade flows so we only settle the difference, dramatically reducing hard-currency demand.
“Now our job is customer education – training branch relationship managers and showing SMEs that they don’t need a domiciliary dollar account to trade with Accra,” said a head of trade finance at a tier-one Nigerian bank in Benin City, who requested anonymity.
The Central Bank of Nigeria and Bank of Ghana use tiered KYC to expand low-value access, while ECOWAS aligns regional payments with the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol and PAPSS adds a currency marketplace for local-currency liquidity.
Success hinges on affordability, reliability, digital literacy, network access, and customer support.
Back at Seme-Krake, Okafor has begun to experience the benefits.
She opened a tiered business account with a Nigerian bank offering mobile PAPSS transfers and attended a digital-literacy workshop.
In August, she completed her first digital invoice settlement from a buyer in Accra, receiving the payment in her Nigerian account before her driver had completed customs clearance.
She still carries CFA francs to pay suppliers in Cotonou because the payment connections she needs across the Nigeria-Benin corridor remain incomplete.
“The phone transfer worked in two minutes, and I didn’t lose a single kobo to street changers.
“If they can make Benin work the exact same way, I won’t ever carry cash across this border again,” she said.
For Nigerian SMEs and their regional counterparts, the value of instant payments extends beyond transaction speed.
It offers the ability to conduct cross-border trade without eroding profit margins through expensive, delayed, and complex payment processes. (NANFeatures)

items.title: Nigeria, 8 other African countries to benefit from $135m health investment

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria, 8 other African countries to benefit from $135m health investment
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Nigeria, 8 other African countries to benefit from $135m health investment
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   28 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Usman Aliyu
Nigeria and eight other African countries are to benefit from a $135 million investment by the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity to improve access to essential medicines, medical equipment and technologies.
The foundation announced the commitment on Thursday at the International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
In a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Thursday, the foundation explained that the investment would support more than 500 health facilities across the nine countries.
The other beneficiaries are Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Rwanda, Ghana, Sierra Leone and Mozambique.
The investment, according to the statement, is expected to mobilise more than $550 million in additional financing through matching contributions from partner governments and donors.
The foundation explained that each participating government would contribute at least an equivalent amount to support the initiative.
It noted that the programme was designed to improve maternal and newborn survival, strengthen primary healthcare and equip health workers with essential supplies needed to deliver quality services.
The foundation said persistent shortages of essential medicines and medical equipment remained a major challenge across African health systems, contributing to treatment delays and undermining healthcare delivery.
It cited estimates indicating that only 35 per cent of essential medicines were available in public health facilities across Africa, while less than one-third of facilities were equipped to conduct basic diagnostic tests.
The foundation said the investment would build on country-led health financing initiatives, using co-financing arrangements to attract additional resources from governments and development partners.
Meanwhile, Dr Shamma Khalifa Al Mazrouei, Director-General of the foundation, said the investment would support governments in ensuring that health workers had reliable access to essential medical supplies.
“In partnership with countries, we are working towards a future where no mother, newborn, or child dies from a preventable cause,” she said.
Al Mazrouei said skilled health workers required adequate medicines and equipment to deliver quality care and improve health outcomes.
In Ethiopia, the foundation committed $20 million to the country’s Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child Health Compact.
The commitment, according to the statement, helped mobilise an additional $151.2 million from development partners, which was matched by the Ethiopian Government, bringing total financing to $342.4 dollars.
The foundation noted that the funding was expected to equip about 120 health facilities over three years with supplies, including artificial intelligence-enabled ultrasound equipment and antibiotics to prevent infections.
In Rwanda, the foundation committed $15 million to provide essential equipment to 170 health facilities, including district and teaching hospitals, while helping mobilise an additional 40 million dollars.
The foundation said the investment would support safer childbirth and newborn care through equipment for managing post-delivery bleeding, incubators and respiratory support for premature and critically ill newborns.
In Liberia, a $10 million commitment, matched by donor funding, was announced to support the country’s national referral teaching hospital and connected health facilities.
The foundation said the intervention would provide technologies for managing complicated births, stabilising critically ill newborns and children, and improving bedside diagnosis
It said the investment would also support clinical mentorship for doctors, nurses and midwives, as well as training in biomedical engineering to strengthen equipment maintenance and repair capacity.
The foundation said the initiative reflected its commitment to strengthening health systems and reducing preventable diseases through partnerships with governments and communities. (NAN)

items.title: Sweden tops 2026 international media freedom support index

original_payload.original_title: Sweden tops 2026 international media freedom support index
original_payload.original_body:
SWEDEN has emerged as the leading country in the 2026 Index on International Media Freedom Support (IMFS), an annual ranking that   assesses governments’ financial, diplomatic and protection-related support for media freedom internationally.
The index assessed 30 countries that are members of both the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD-DAC) Development Assistance Committee and the Media Freedom Coalition (MFC).
It evaluated countries’ support for media freedom outside their borders through diplomatic engagement, funding for media development, and initiatives to protect journalists at risk and those in exile.
The findings raise concerns about the sustainability of international support for independent journalism at a time when media organisations face increasing threats, financial pressures and attacks on journalists.
Although the report does not assess Africa, countries, including Nigeria, the giant of Africa and other countries outside the index’s assessment face the challenge of sustaining journalism that serves the public interest amid financial pressures and threats to media freedom.

items.title: Adeleke begins second term, pledges to transform Osun economy

original_payload.original_title: Adeleke begins second term, pledges to transform Osun economy
original_payload.original_body:
OSUN State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been sworn in for a second term in office, promising to move the state away from its dependence on the civil service towards an industrialised economy through investments in agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and job creation.
Adeleke made the promise on Friday, November 27, 2026, after he and his deputy, Kola Adewusi, took their oaths of office at the Osogbo Township Stadium, marking the beginning of another four-year tenure.
The Chief Judge of Osun State, Oyebola Adepele-Ojo, administered the oaths and President Bola Tinubu was represented at the ceremony by Vice-President Kashim Shettima.
“My vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one. We are open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment,” he said during his inaugural address.
Adeleke thanked residents for renewing his mandate and pledged that his administration would focus on improving citizens’ welfare, expanding infrastructure, strengthening the digital economy, promoting agricultural development and creating employment opportunities, particularly for young people.

items.title: Journée internationale de l’aide humanitaire : Le Bénin et ses partenaires célèbrent l’évènement

original_payload.original_title: Journée internationale de l’aide humanitaire : Le Bénin et ses partenaires célèbrent l’évènement
original_payload.original_body:
La nouvelle cité administrative de la ville de Parakou a accueilli, jeudi 26 novembre 2026, les manifestations officielles entrant dans le cadre de la célébration de la Journée mondiale de l’aide humanitaire, couplée avec la Journée des Nations Unies. La cérémonie a été présidée par Madame Mariam CHABI TALATA, Vice-présidente de la République, en présence du Ministre délégué auprès du Président de la République chargé de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, représentant le gouvernement. Les acteurs humanitaires, sous la houlette de la Coordonnatrice résidente du Système des Nations Unies au Bénin, ainsi que les organisations non gouvernementales nationales et internationales, ont également pris part à ces manifestations.
« Agir pour l’humanité ». C’est le thème retenu cette année pour la célébration en différé au Bénin de la Journée internationale de l’aide humanitaire, couplée avec celle des Nations Unies. Pour le Ministre en charge de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, ces trois mots, en apparence simples, portent une exigence immense : « celle de ne jamais détourner le regard face à la souffrance humaine, de ne pas laisser une personne seule face à l’épreuve et de faire de la solidarité non pas une simple intention, mais une action concrète ».
La situation actuelle du Bénin exige une vigilance constante. Le pays dénombrait en effet, au 30 septembre 2026, 34 355 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile, dont 22 206 réfugiés et 12 149 demandeurs d’asile. Face à ces défis, Djibril MAMA CISSE MOUSSA a mis en avant les efforts du gouvernement : le renforcement du dispositif de prévention et de gestion des urgences, une réponse adaptée aux personnes déplacées et réfugiées, une meilleure synergie entre l’État, les collectivités territoriales, les organisations humanitaires et les partenaires, ainsi que la prise en compte des communautés hôtes.
À la tribune de l'évènement, la Vice-présidente de la République a réaffirmé l’engagement de l’État béninois à agir pour apporter de meilleures réponses aux peines et souffrances des personnes déplacées. Sous l’impulsion du Président WADAGNI, le Bénin a franchi une étape décisive dans la planification de son développement. Il revient donc à chaque acteur du développement de rester aux côtés des populations ainsi qu’à leur écoute, pour les aider à résoudre leurs problèmes quotidiens. « La dimension humanitaire de la présente journée donne à notre responsabilité un écho particulier. Célébrer la Journée mondiale de l’aide humanitaire dans le septentrion béninois, région où nos populations et celles des pays voisins sont en proie aux menaces terroristes, est très pertinent et significatif pour tous », a-t-elle souligné. Elle a également salué les familles d’accueil et les communautés qui ouvrent leurs portes aux personnes déplacées, ainsi que tous les acteurs humanitaires mobilisés.
La coordonnatrice résidente du Système des Nations Unies au Bénin, Madame Aminatou SAR, est aussi intervenue au cours de la cérémonie pour porter la voix de toutes les agences onusiennes et de l'ensemble des organisations humanitaires intervenant dans le pays. Selon elle, le sens de l’action collective des agences n’est pas de multiplier les projets, mais de transformer durablement les conditions de vie des populations. En 2025, a-t-elle déclaré, l’apport du Système des Nations Unies aux réponses d’urgence a permis à plus de 62 000 enfants et à plus de 3 000 familles de bénéficier d’un appui en matière d’eau, d’hygiène et de dignité. Elle a rendu hommage au gouvernement, aux acteurs humanitaires et aux populations hôtes. Pour finir, Madame Aminatou SAR a mis en exergue le rôle de l’Agence béninoise de protection civile, dont la mission est de coordonner l’ensemble des interventions à caractère humanitaire au Bénin.
Les manifestations se poursuivent avec une exposition dans la cour de la cité administrative de Parakou. L’ensemble des délégations est par ailleurs appelé à se rendre, vendredi 27 novembre 2026, dans la commune de Kalalé (Arrondissement de Dérassi), pour une remise symbolique d’assistance aux personnes déplacées et en situation de vulnérabilité.

items.title: Dérives numériques : le Cnin livre un tiktokeur à la justice

original_payload.original_title: Dérives numériques : le Cnin livre un tiktokeur à la justice
original_payload.original_body:
Le Centre national d’investigations numériques    (Cnin)     annonce l’interpellation d’un internaute identifié par les initiales O.S., à la suite d’une publication sur TikTok. Plusieurs dispositions de la législation béninoise seraient concernées, notamment celles relatives aux pratiques de sorcellerie, aux communications électroniques intimidantes et à la diffusion de contenus liés à une infraction.
Une publication sur TikTok conduit son auteur présumé devant la justice. Le Centre national d’investigations numériques (CNIN) a annoncé l’interpellation de O.S., à la suite de la diffusion d’un contenu sur cette plateforme. Selon l’institution, la publication incriminée contreviendrait à plusieurs dispositions légales en vigueur au Bénin. L’intéressé a été mis à la disposition de la justice, à qui revient désormais la responsabilité d’apprécier les faits et de se prononcer sur son cas.
Dans sa communication, le CNIN fait notamment référence à l’article 458 du Code pénal. Cette disposition réprime les pratiques de sorcellerie, de magie ou de charlatanisme lorsqu’elles sont susceptibles de troubler l’ordre public ou de porter atteinte aux personnes. L’institution évoque également le Code du numérique, qui prévoit des sanctions contre certaines communications électroniques à caractère intimidant ainsi que contre la diffusion d’images liées à une infraction.
Ces dispositions constituent les fondements juridiques avancés par le CNIN pour justifier son intervention dans cette affaire.
Des comportements numériques aux conséquences judiciaires
Au-delà de cette interpellation, le Centre national d’investigations numériques entend attirer l’attention sur les comportements susceptibles de tomber sous le coup de la loi dans l’environnement numérique. Les réseaux sociaux occupent désormais une place importante dans les habitudes de communication. Ils permettent de s’informer, de partager des expériences, de développer des activités et de saisir des opportunités. La majorité des utilisateurs en font un usage responsable.
Toutefois, certaines pratiques observées sur ces plateformes peuvent porter atteinte aux droits et à la dignité d’autrui.Le CNIN cite plusieurs exemples de dérives. Il s’agit notamment des rituels transformés en menaces publiques, des directs au cours desquels des personnes se dénudent dans le but d’attirer des vues, de la diffusion de contenus pour adultes, des vidéos de personnes filmées à leur insu et des campagnes d’acharnement dirigées contre des individus désignés.
Ces publications ne relèvent pas toutes nécessairement de la même qualification juridique. Leur contenu, leur contexte et leurs conséquences déterminent les dispositions susceptibles de leur être applicables.Derrière ces pratiques, l’institution souligne surtout les préjudices que peuvent subir les personnes exposées. Une vidéo diffusée sans consentement, une publication humiliante ou des propos assimilables à des menaces peuvent affecter la réputation, la tranquillité et la sécurité d’une victime. La viralité des contenus sur les plateformes numériques peut amplifier ces atteintes et prolonger leurs conséquences.
Le partage engage aussi la responsabilité des internautes
Le CNIN met également en garde contre une pratique souvent banalisée sur les réseaux sociaux : le relais de contenus problématiques. En effet, la responsabilité d’un internaute ne se limite pas nécessairement à la création ou à la publication initiale d’un contenu. Le fait de le partager ou de contribuer à sa diffusion peut également engager sa responsabilité lorsque le contenu est illicite.
Cette mise en garde concerne particulièrement les utilisateurs qui relaient des vidéos choquantes, des images portant atteinte à la vie privée ou des publications visant à intimider et à humilier une personne. Le nombre de vues, les commentaires ou les réactions suscités par une publication ne sauraient justifier sa diffusion lorsque celle-ci porte atteinte aux droits d’autrui ou contrevient à la législation.
Un appel à la vigilance collective
Pour prévenir ces dérives, le Centre invite les internautes à adopter des comportements plus responsables dans leurs interactions numériques. Il recommande notamment de prendre le temps de réfléchir avant de publier ou de partager un contenu, afin d’en mesurer les conséquences possibles. Le signalement auprès du CNIN des publications jugées problématiques figure également parmi les moyens d’action proposés.
L’objectif affiché est de favoriser un environnement numérique plus sûr, dans lequel les possibilités offertes par les réseaux sociaux ne se transforment pas en instruments de menace, d’humiliation ou d’exposition abusive des personnes.

items.title: Leadership féminin au Bénin : 80 femmes leaders créent un réseau de solidarité durable

original_payload.original_title: Leadership féminin au Bénin : 80 femmes leaders créent un réseau de solidarité durable
original_payload.original_body:
Quatre-vingt femmes leaders de l’Atlantique et du Littoral veulent renforcer leur solidarité et développer des partenariats durables. Réunies les 19 et 20 novembre 2026 à Ouidah, elles ont participé à un atelier de réseautage. L’initiative du Consortium RIFONGA-WANEP-FENEP vise à rompre leur isolement et mutualiser leurs compétences. Elle ambitionne également de prolonger les acquis des programmes de promotion du leadership féminin au Bénin.
Faire de la solidarité féminine un levier d’action collective. C’est l’ambition portée par 80 femmes leaders réunies à Ouidah. Les participantes ont pris part à un atelier de réseautage à l’hôtel Terra Nostra.
Organisée les 19 et 20 novembre 2026, cette rencontre a rassemblé des bénéficiaires de plusieurs programmes. Parmi elles figurent notamment les participantes au Programme d’Appui à l’Égalité de Genre (PAEG 1).
Le Consortium RIFONGA-WANEP-FENEP (CRWF) a initié cette rencontre pour répondre à un défi précis. Malgré leurs différentes formations, les femmes leaders évoluent souvent dans des réseaux distincts. Cette dispersion fragilise parfois leurs relations après la clôture des projets.
Le Consortium veut donc dépasser les cadres individuels des programmes. Il entend construire un réseau commun, fondé sur l’entraide, le partage d’expériences et la coopération.
Un appel à dépasser l’isolement des femmes leaders
Plusieurs personnalités ont pris part à la cérémonie d’ouverture. Il s’agit notamment de Sabine J. FOURN, première adjointe au maire de Ouidah. Elle représentait le maire à cette occasion.
L’honorable députée Alimatou BADAROU a également assisté à la rencontre. Sadia Adébiyi ADAM, vice-présidente de RIFONGA-Bénin, représentait la cheffe de file du Consortium. Prudencia HOUNOU représentait la Directrice départementale de la Famille et de l’Action sociale de l’Atlantique.
Dans son allocution, Sadia Adébiyi ADAM a précisé l’objectif de cette initiative. Selon elle, les participantes n’avaient pas besoin d’une formation supplémentaire. Elles devaient surtout établir des relations avec d’autres femmes déjà formées et engagées.
« Si nous sommes ici, c’est pour répondre à un défi majeur : celui de l’isolement », a-t-elle déclaré.
Elle a invité les participantes à privilégier la coopération plutôt que la compétition. Elle les a également encouragées à construire un réseau d’entraide. Celui-ci devra faciliter l’accès aux conseils, au soutien et aux opportunités.
Pour structurer cette dynamique, plusieurs outils sont envisagés. Le Consortium prévoit notamment un annuaire dynamique des participantes. Une charte de fonctionnement et un plan d’action conjoint figurent également parmi les perspectives. La désignation de points focaux complète ces propositions.
Prenant la parole au nom du maire, Sabine J. FOURN a insisté sur l’exercice des responsabilités. Elle estime que les femmes doivent pleinement assumer leurs fonctions dans les instances décisionnelles.
« Nous ne devons pas seulement préparer les femmes à accéder aux espaces de décision, nous devons également les préparer à y exercer une influence positive, à assumer leurs responsabilités et à produire des résultats », a-t-elle affirmé.
Pour sa part, Alimatou BADAROU a encouragé les participantes à transformer leurs échanges en partenariats concrets. Elle a également insisté sur la collecte de leurs expériences, difficultés et attentes.
Prudencia HOUNOU a rappelé l’importance des échanges dans le renforcement des capacités féminines. Elle a souligné le rôle de l’apprentissage mutuel dans la consolidation des acquis. La représentante de la Direction départementale a ensuite officiellement ouvert les travaux.
Des compétences et des expériences mises en commun
Durant les deux jours, les participantes ont pris part à plusieurs activités pratiques. Les organisateurs ont notamment proposé des exercices de connaissance mutuelle. Un marché des compétences, des cercles de mentorat et un World Café ont également rythmé les travaux.
Ces activités ont permis aux femmes de présenter leurs expériences et leurs domaines d’expertise. Elles ont aussi identifié des possibilités de collaboration entre leurs différentes organisations.
Cette démarche a reçu un accueil favorable auprès des participantes. Sybille Houeton Ogoua, juriste et chargée de projet d’autonomisation au sein du réseau WILDAF-Bénin, a salué l’initiative. Bénéficiaire du programme Jeune Leader de la Fondation Friedrich-Ebert, elle a insisté sur l’intérêt de fédérer les efforts.
« Je voudrais surtout saluer cette approche qui consiste à fédérer les efforts plutôt qu’à travailler de manière isolée », a-t-elle souligné.
Elle estime que la mutualisation des ressources renforcera l’efficacité des interventions. Cette approche pourrait également favoriser leur pérennité.
Confort Fanou, bénéficiaire du PAEG dans le département du Littoral, partage cette satisfaction. Elle retient particulièrement les nouvelles perspectives professionnelles offertes par les rencontres.
« Personnellement, cette rencontre m’a permis d’élargir davantage mon réseau professionnel et de nouer de nouveaux contacts », a-t-elle confié.
Elle espère désormais transformer ces nouvelles relations en opportunités de collaboration.
Une dynamique de réseautage étendue à l’Ouémé et au Plateau
Le Consortium RIFONGA-WANEP-FENEP entend prolonger les relations nouées pendant cet atelier. Son ambition consiste à mettre en place un réseau organisé et durable. Celui-ci pourra porter des initiatives communes au bénéfice des femmes et de leurs communautés.
Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre du PAEG 1. La Coopération suisse au Bénin apporte son appui financier. Particip GmbH assure, pour sa part, l’accompagnement technique.
Le projet s’inscrit également dans la dynamique du Cadre de Concertation pour la Synergie d’Action autour de la promotion du Leadership Féminin (CCSA-LF).
Dans cette continuité, le Consortium a organisé une deuxième rencontre les 23 et 24 novembre 2026 à Kétou. Cette session a ciblé les bénéficiaires des programmes de leadership féminin de l’Ouémé et du Plateau.
L’initiative vise donc à élargir progressivement les connexions entre les femmes leaders. Elle entend faire de leurs expériences individuelles une ressource collective au service de leurs engagements.

items.title: PRESS RELEASE: SRSG Remarks at the Launch of the AU-IGAD-UN Joint Task Force

original_payload.original_title: PRESS RELEASE: SRSG Remarks at the Launch of the AU-IGAD-UN Joint Task Force
original_payload.original_body:
Home
Press releases
PRESS RELEASE: SRSG Remarks at the Launch of the AU-IGAD-UN Joint Task Force
PRESS RELEASE: SRSG Remarks at the Launch of the AU-IGAD-UN Joint Task Force
27 November 2026
JUBA -  Chairperson of the AU Commission, His Excellency Mahmoud Ali Youssouf;
African Union High Representative for the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea, and Chairperson of the Joint Task Force, His Excellency Jakaya Kikwete;
Caretaker Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Republic of South Sudan;
Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security of the African Union Commission and moderator of this opening session, Ambassador Bankole Adeoye; IGAD Special Envoy for South Sudan, H.E. Ambassador Moussa Djama Ali;
Special Envoy Cong;
Excellencies, distinguished representatives, colleagues, ladies and gentlemen:
Good morning.
I thank the African Union Commission for hosting this launch and commend the AU C5+, His Excellency President Jakaya Kikwete and IGAD for their sustained commitment to South Sudan.
The world’s youngest country is currently on the difficult path of nation-building, facing political, security and humanitarian challenges. The AU Chair has been clear on what our priorities should be moving ahead, and we will not lose sight of the opportunities that exist to advance peace and stability in South Sudan.
Excellencies, colleagues,
For the United Nations, the launch of the AU–IGAD–UN Joint Task Force is an important milestone in supporting the African Union High Representative. It comes at a time when aligning our efforts is essential. We thus welcome the opportunity to exchange views and jointly explore how best to support his engagement, drawing on our complementary mandates, experience and comparative advantages, will be key.
We are clear: there is no substitute for a political solution grounded in dialogue, compromise and national ownership. Building broad consensus will require meaningful and inclusive engagement among all stakeholders on the way forward.
Honourable Minister, we welcome your presence with us today. We also welcome the Presidential Decree on humanitarian access, whose implementation would help facilitate humanitarian assistance to people in need. Sustained Government engagement and commitment will be vital to the success of our collective support efforts. We look forward to working closely with the Government on shared priorities, practical steps and follow-through. South Sudanese ownership and leadership is indispensable to durable peace.
Excellencies, colleagues,
Elections are an important milestone, but not an end to the peace process. Their value lies in contributing to peace and stability. Lasting stability also requires respect for the ceasefire, inclusive governance and implementation of outstanding peace agreement commitments, ranging from a permanent constitution and transitional security arrangements to judicial reform, transitional justice and national reconciliation.
The United Nations stands ready to contribute through its good offices, political engagement, joint assessments and preventive diplomacy, in close partnership with the AU and IGAD.
Ultimately, the people of South Sudan must remain at the heart of our efforts - their safety, dignity and voice is essential in shaping their future. And our success must be measured by the tangible changes we help deliver in the lives of the women, men and children of South Sudan that we serve.
I look forward to our discussions today and to deepening our shared support for lasting peace in South Sudan.
I thank you.
--
Contact: UNMISS Chief of Communication and Public Information, Francesca Mold      mold2@un.org      or      unmiss-spokesperson@un.org

items.title: Lac : le PNUD renforce les capacités opérationnelles de l’administration locale

original_payload.original_title: Lac : le PNUD renforce les capacités opérationnelles de l’administration locale
original_payload.original_body:
Le Programme des Nations unies pour le développement (PNUD) a remis, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, à l’administration provinciale du Lac un important lot d’équipements d’une valeur estimée à 160 millions de FCFA, dans le cadre de la Facilité régionale de stabilisation.
La cérémonie, présidée par le délégué général du gouvernement auprès de la province du Lac, le général Saleh Haggar Tidjani, a été marquée par la remise de cinq véhicules, de seize motos tout-terrain et de deux kits de connexion satellitaire Starlink. Ces équipements sont destinés aux services administratifs et judiciaires ainsi qu’aux forces de défense et de sécurité.
Selon le chef du bureau du PNUD à Bol, Henri Mashagiro, cet appui vise à améliorer la mobilité des services publics, à renforcer leur efficacité sur le terrain et à consolider la présence de l’État dans les zones les plus éloignées de la province.

items.title: Tchad-Chine : l'ENA s'inspire du modèle de développement de Pékin pour former ses futurs cadres

original_payload.original_title: Tchad-Chine : l'ENA s'inspire du modèle de développement de Pékin pour former ses futurs cadres
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad-Chine : l'ENA s'inspire du modèle de développement de Pékin pour former ses futurs cadres
L'ENA du Tchad a accueilli une conférence de haut niveau sur le modèle de développement chinois, marquée par un don de matériel de l'ambassade de Chine.
Alwihda Info
27 nov. 2026
Par Ahmad Youssouf Ali
L’École nationale d’administration (ENA) du Tchad a organisé, le mercredi 25 novembre 2026, une conférence-débat de haut niveau placée sous le thème : « L’expérience du développement de la Chine : quelles inspirations pour le Tchad ? ». Cette rencontre, inscrite dans le cycle des « Grands Rendez-vous de l’ENA », s'est déroulée en présence de l’ambassadeur de la République populaire de Chine au Tchad, Wang Xining, et d’une importante délégation.
L’objectif affiché était d’offrir aux futurs cadres de l’administration publique tchadienne une compréhension approfondie des étapes clés du développement chinois, des moteurs de sa croissance économique et des leçons transposables au contexte tchadien.
En préambule des échanges, l’ambassade de Chine a procédé à une remise de matériel au profit de l’ENA. Ce lot, comprenant des équipements informatiques, bureautiques et des outils de travail, a été réceptionné par le directeur général de l’institution, le Dr Mahamat Borgou Hassan, entouré de ses proches collaborateurs. Le directeur général a salué ce geste, y voyant la preuve tangible de l’engagement de Pékin en faveur de l’enseignement supérieur tchadien. De son côté, le diplomate chinois a qualifié cette dotation de première étape dans l’appui de sa mission diplomatique à l’école, tout en réitérant la volonté de son pays d’accompagner durablement la prospérité du Tchad.
La cérémonie s’est poursuivie par la conférence-débat proprement dite, modérée par le Dr Issa Doubragne, directeur général du Fonds spécial de préparation des projets d’infrastructures, enseignant-chercheur et ancien ministre. Cet échange a rassemblé des élèves, le personnel de l’ENA ainsi que diverses personnalités politiques et administratives.
La délégation chinoise a retracé la trajectoire économique menant la Chine au rang de deuxième puissance mondiale, en illustrant son propos par des exemples concrets d’industrialisation. Les intervenants ont exploré des pistes pour valoriser le potentiel agricole tchadien à la lumière de l’expérience chinoise. La partie chinoise a réitéré sa disposition à soutenir le Tchad dans la production et la transformation agricole, en tenant compte des spécificités climatiques locales, dans le cadre d’un renforcement de la coopération bilatérale.
Le discours d’ouverture a été prononcé par l’ambassadeur Wang Xining. Les exposés thématiques ont ensuite rythmé les travaux : M. Liu Junkai, attaché politique, est intervenu sur la politique de réforme et d’ouverture de la Chine ; Mme Fan Xinmu, attachée politique, a abordé le développement agricole ; et Mme Yang Sihan, attachée commerciale, a exposé les enjeux de la construction industrielle. M. Sun Rui, attaché commercial, a quant à lui assuré la coordination logistique et la remise des certificats.
Afin de permettre à un public élargi de suivre ces travaux diplomatiques et académiques, l’ENA a indiqué que l’événement a été retransmis en direct sur sa page Facebook officielle.

items.title: Gabon : une fausse capitaine de la Marine interpellée avec trois millions de FCFA de stupéfiants

original_payload.original_title: Gabon : une fausse capitaine de la Marine interpellée avec trois millions de FCFA de stupéfiants
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Gabon : une fausse capitaine de la Marine interpellée avec trois millions de FCFA de stupéfiants
Une fausse capitaine de la Marine nationale a été interpellée au Gabon en possession de stupéfiants d'une valeur de trois millions de FCFA dissimulés dans de la farine de manioc.
Alwihda Info
27 nov. 2026
© DR
Par Temandang Gontran
Une ressortissante congolaise a été interpellée le 19 novembre 2026 à Lébamba, dans la province de la Ngounié, au Gabon. Elle est soupçonnée d'usurpation d'identité militaire, de faux et usage de faux, de trafic de stupéfiants et de vente illicite de véhicules, rapportent plusieurs médias gabonais.
D'après les premiers éléments de l'enquête, la suspecte se faisait passer pour une capitaine de la Marine nationale gabonaise. Pour tromper la vigilance des forces de l'ordre, elle arborait un treillis militaire et présentait de faux documents, lui permettant ainsi de franchir les barrages routiers sans éveiller les soupçons.
Les enquêteurs indiquent que cette stratégie aurait évolué au fil du temps. La mise en cause se serait d'abord présentée comme lieutenant avant d'endosser le grade supérieur de capitaine de la Marine.
Lors de son arrestation, les gendarmes ont fouillé son véhicule. La fouille a permis de découvrir plusieurs bottes de chanvre indien ainsi qu'une centaine de plaquettes de tramadol, astucieusement dissimulées dans des sacs de foufou (farine de manioc). Selon les autorités, la valeur marchande de ces produits stupéfiants est estimée à près de 3 millions de FCFA.
Les investigations se poursuivent afin de déterminer l'étendue du réseau criminel et d'identifier d'éventuels complices impliqués dans ce trafic transfrontalier entre le Congo et le Gabon.

items.title: تشاد: مركزية تراخيص تصدير الذهب والمواد المعدنية عبر النافذة الواحدة

original_payload.original_title: تشاد: مركزية تراخيص تصدير الذهب والمواد المعدنية عبر النافذة الواحدة
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
تشاد: مركزية تراخيص تصدير الذهب والمواد المعدنية عبر النافذة الواحدة
أكدت النافذة الواحدة لتصدير الذهب والمواد المعدنية في تشاد أن إصدار تراخيص التصدير بات حصرياً بيدها، في خطوة تهدف إلى ضبط قطاع التعدين ومركزية الإجراءات.
Alwihda Info
27 nov. 2026
Illustration © Pixabay
ذكرت النافذة الواحدة لتصدير الذهب والمواد المعدنية الأخرى (GUEOSM)، في بيان رسمي، أن إصدار جميع التراخيص المتعلقة بالمواد المعدنية أصبح يندرج حصرياً ضمن صلاحياتها.
وتشمل هذه الإجراءات بشكل خاص الذهب، الفضة، الماس، الأنتيمون، التنجستن، فضلاً عن نفايات النحاس. وتهدف هذه الخطوة إلى التأطير الصارم للقطاع ومركزية الإجراءات الإدارية.
إجراءات حصرية جديدة
وفقاً للتوجيهات التي وقعها المنسق العام، محمد سليمان شرف:
1. إيداع الملفات: يجب إيداع أي طلب للحصول على ترخيص حصرياً لدى تنسيقية النافذة الواحدة.
2. حصرية الإصدار: لا يحق لأي هيكل أو مصلحة أو شخص آخر إصدار أو الوعود بإصدار هذا النوع من التراخيص.
3. الصلاحية: يُعتبر أي مستند يتم الحصول عليه خارج هذا الإطار الرسمي باطلاً وكأن لم يكن.
وتدعو التنسيقية كافة المتعاملين الاقتصاديين، والمصدرين، والفاعلين في قطاع التعدين إلى الامتثال الصارم لهذه التوجيهات.

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : centralisation des autorisations pour l'exportation de l'or et des substances minérales
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : centralisation des autorisations pour l'exportation de l'or et des substances minérales
Au Tchad, le Guichet unique d'exportation de l'or et des substances minérales devient la seule instance habilitée à délivrer les autorisations pour le secteur.
Alwihda Info
27 nov. 2026
Illustration © Pixabay
Le Guichet Unique d'Exportation de l'Or et autres Substances Minérales (GUEOSM) a rappelé, par voie de communiqué, que la délivrance de l'ensemble des autorisations relatives aux substances minérales relève désormais de sa compétence exclusive.
Sont notamment concernés l'or, l'argent, le diamant, l'antimoine, le tungstène ainsi que les déchets de cuivre. Cette mesure vise à encadrer strictement le secteur et à centraliser les procédures administratives.
Des procédures désormais exclusives
Selon les directives signées par le Coordonnateur général, Mahamat Souleyman Charf :
1. Dépôt des dossiers : Toute demande d'autorisation doit impérativement être déposée auprès de la Coordination du Guichet Unique.
2. Exclusivité de délivrance : Aucune autre structure, service ou personne n'est habilité à délivrer ou à promettre ce type d'autorisation.
3. Validité : Tout document obtenu en dehors de ce cadre officiel sera considéré comme nul et non avenu.
La Coordination invite l'ensemble des opérateurs économiques, exportateurs et acteurs du secteur minier à se conformer strictement à ces dispositions.

Tchad : Le projet FLUVIAC au cœur des échanges sur le commerce du bétail et de la viande
admin
novembre 27, 2026
2 minutes lues
91 vues
La deuxième journée de la rencontre de concertation consacrée à la formulation du Projet d’appui à la fluidification des échanges de bétail et de viande en Afrique centrale (FLUVIAC) s’est tenue ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à N’Djaména.
Organisée par la Commission économique du bétail, de la viande et des ressources halieutiques ( CEBEVIHRA ), elle vise à recueillir les contributions des acteurs de la chaîne de valeur pour mieux préparer la mise en œuvre du projet.
Présidant la cérémonie d’ouverture, le point focal du ministère de l’Élevage et de la Production animale, Dr Abakar Mahamat Nour Mallaye, a salué cette initiative qu’il considère comme importante pour le Tchad.
Il a rappelé que le pays dispose d’un cheptel estimé à plus de 156 millions de têtes, toutes espèces confondues. Selon lui, le Tchad représente à lui seul 85 % du cheptel de la zone CEMAC, ce qui lui confère une place importante dans les échanges de bétail et de viande en Afrique centrale.
Le responsable a ainsi invité les participants à mettre à profit les travaux pour apporter des contributions concrètes à la formulation du projet, qui concerne l’ensemble des pays de la CEMAC.
À travers cette concertation, les parties prenantes sont appelées à réfléchir aux moyens de faciliter les échanges commerciaux et de mieux valoriser le potentiel de l’élevage dans la sous-région.

La 10ᵉ édition du festival Koura Gosso se tient dans le département de Lac Wey autour du thème : « Inspirer, rassembler, partager : art et entrepreneuriat écologique pour demain ». Organisé par l’association « Femmes Aussi », cet événement culturel met en avant la créativité, la paix, la cohésion sociale et l’entrepreneuriat des jeunes et des femmes.
À travers cette édition, les organisateurs veulent promouvoir les arts, valoriser le patrimoine culturel et offrir aux jeunes un espace d’expression et d’apprentissage, notamment à travers les danses traditionnelles.
Prenant la parole au nom de la directrice du festival, Djinodji Calvin a souligné le rôle des jeunes artistes dans la promotion de la paix et de la cohésion sociale. Il a également insisté sur l’importance de transmettre les danses traditionnelles aux générations futures.
Pour sa part, Netoua Ernestine, présidente de l’association «  Femmes Aussi  » et directrice artistique du festival, a rappelé que la danse est un langage universel qui rassemble les communautés au-delà de leurs différences culturelles, religieuses et sociales.
Après dix années d’efforts, de réussites et de difficultés, elle entend faire de la culture un véritable levier de développement, capable de créer des activités économiques et de favoriser l’autonomisation des jeunes et des femmes.
Le préfet du Lac Wey, Mbairam Alladoum, a salué cette initiative, qu’il considère comme une source de fierté pour la province. Il a rappelé que la culture ne se limite pas au divertissement, mais constitue aussi un moyen de renforcer la paix et le vivre-ensemble.
À travers cette 10ᵉ édition, le festival Koura Gosso entend ainsi faire de la culture un outil de cohésion sociale, de valorisation du patrimoine et de développement durable.

Le Réseau des jeunes entrepreneurs du Tchad (RJET) a organisé, ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, un point de presse à N’Djaména pour présenter la 5ᵉ édition de la Semaine de l’entrepreneuriat des jeunes Tchadiens. Placée sous le thème : « Jeunesse, innovation et industrialisation : bâtir les champions économiques du Tchad ».
Cette initiative est organisée sous le haut patronage du ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports.
À cette occasion, la présidente du RJET, Mangueal Prisca, a réaffirmé l’engagement du réseau à accompagner les jeunes dans leurs initiatives entrepreneuriales. Elle a souligné que la jeunesse tchadienne représente une véritable force économique capable de contribuer au développement du pays.
Cette 5ᵉ édition prévoit deux grandes phases. La première, du 19 au 31 octobre 2026, a été consacrée à des ateliers et à des formations pratiques destinés à renforcer les compétences des jeunes entrepreneurs.
La seconde, prévue du 1ᵉʳ au 6 novembre 2026, portera sur une exposition réunissant des entrepreneurs, des porteurs de projets, des PME et différents acteurs de l’écosystème entrepreneurial.
À travers cette activité, le RJET entend créer un cadre de formation, de partage d’expériences et de promotion des initiatives des jeunes, tout en encourageant l’innovation et leur contribution au développement économique du Tchad.

Au nom de la directrice générale, Menodji Rita, Ronelngue Nangtoingar a appelé les femmes et les filles à briser le silence face aux violences.
Cette campagne vise à renforcer la sensibilisation et la mobilisation collective pour la protection des droits des femmes et des filles au Tchad.

Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced the proposal on Friday during the “Food from Ukraine” conference, saying Kyiv was ready to restore freedom of navigation and ensure the uninterrupted export of agricultural products.

He accused Russia of repeatedly putting forward “unrealistic demands” in response to Kyiv’s proposals, according to Suspilne, Ukraine’s national broadcaster.
The Ukrainian proposal was being considered, as Russian President Vladimir Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony for a new nuclear-powered submarine, which Moscow claims is the first to be equipped with Russia’s Zircon hypersonic missile. Putin said he was confident that plans to build a powerful naval force would be implemented on time and in full, Russian news agencies reported.
Previous attempts at a ceasefire

Ukraine and Russia are both  major agricultural exporters , and attacks on vessels and port infrastructure have disrupted shipments transiting through the Black Sea.

items.title: Mecca pact allies condemn ‘heinous’ Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia

original_payload.original_body:
Senior government and defence officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have denounced the continuing attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on Saudi Arabia and renewed their pledge to support the kingdom in safeguarding its security and sovereignty.
The statement followed a meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the  Mecca defence pact  countries in the Pakistani capital, Islamabad, on Friday.

The three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on  August 7,  under which an armed attack on one member is treated as an attack on all three. The committee comprises the three nations’ foreign and defence ministers alongside top military officials.
Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar thanked the participating officials after the roughly two-and-a-half-hour meeting.
“The SPDC meeting reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards regional peace, security and stability,” he told reporters.
“The three sides reiterated their strong condemnation of the persistent and heinous attacks by the Houthi militia, targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” he said.
“They reaffirmed their collective resolve to continue and intensify efforts to support the kingdom in safeguarding its security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, in accordance with the collective defence provisions of the Mecca Agreement for Joint Defence.”

items.title: ‘Bear trap’: Ukraine hails new operation as Russian casualties mount

original_payload.original_title: ‘Bear trap’: Ukraine hails new operation as Russian casualties mount
original_payload.original_body:
Ukraine’s forces liberated more of their land as Russia broke new casualty records and United States negotiators tried to convince Kyiv to give up territory, or NATO membership.
Details emerged on November 20 of a new operation – the fourth this year – in which Ukraine said it cleared Russian troops out of hundreds of square kilometres of land they occupied, this time in the northern Kharkiv region.

That was about a month after Russia said it had encircled 2,000 Ukrainian troops in an enclave adjacent to the Russian border, around the town of Velykyi Burluk.
Ukrainian commanders realised that the troops were in danger of being encircled, and ordered the execution of “Operation Bear Trap”, which relied on deceptive moves and secrecy to attack the enemy from various sides, concealing its main direction.
Ukrainian forces used a Russian T-80 tank and an Abrams M-1 tank to attack the border town of Vilhuvatka, giving the impression that their main blow would land there.
They then attacked Russian reinforcements from the rear as they arrived to shore up defences, and used drones to remotely mine Russian resupply routes.
The Ukrainian command said Operation Bear Trap has so far succeeded in liberating 200sq km (77sq miles) and 14 settlements, and was ongoing.
Russian troops continue to occupy at least four border villages in Kharkiv, including Vovchansk, but their plan to seize almost 500sq km (193sq miles) has been foiled.
It is not the first time Ukrainian forces preempted a Russian pincer movement.

Following the October 27 election, the leader of the centrist Yashar party has been tapped by Israel’s president to form a new government but has so far struggled to put together a ruling coalition.

Yashar negotiators have also held talks with Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud party over the possibility of forming a national unity government involving both parties – without any breakthrough.
