items.title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, halts flights and ticket sales

original_payload.original_title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, halts flights and ticket sales
original_payload.original_body:
Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic said it would file for bankruptcy for its main Norwegian operating unit and has stopped selling tickets, becoming the latest airline casualty of fuel-cost spikes stemming from the war in Iran..
The airline has cancelled all flights and said on its website that its customer service department is no longer available.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Nationwide ground stop could cost US airlines hundreds of millions
list 2 of 4  Belgium’s airports set to shut down due to anti-austerity strike
list 3 of 4  Israeli minister approves return of Flydubai flights to Tel Aviv

end of list
The shutdown came quickly. On Wednesday, the airline, which was founded in 2021, said its financial situation was “critical”. A day later, it suspended flights and warned that it could file for bankruptcy if it failed to secure funding.
By Friday, the airline said it could not raise the money it needed to continue flying.
Norse is the latest airline to struggle with rising fuel costs brought on by the US-led war in Iran. Latvia’s airBaltic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, while  US budget airline Spirit Airlines  went out of business in May.
Jet fuel prices have risen 71 percent globally over the past year and more than 78 percent in Europe, according to the International Air Transport Association (IATA) which tracks jet fuel prices.
“We were unable to absorb the extra cost … Fuel is what toppled this company,” CEO Eivind Roald told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK.
Norse said on its website that passengers could seek refunds through the bankruptcy process but warned that refunds were not guaranteed. It advised customers to check their travel insurance or contact their banks.
“This is a very hard day for the pilots and their families, and for all other Norse employees. Our thoughts are also with the passengers whose journeys are now cancelled,” the board of the Norse Atlantic Pilots Association told the Reuters news agency.

original_payload.original_body:
US President Donald Trump has backed Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s drive to stop oil smuggling and assert state authority, moves that have put Baghdad in direct confrontation with Kurdish authorities and Iran-aligned militias.
Trump said in a Truth Social post on Friday that Washington supports al-Zaidi’s efforts to “stop the smuggling of Iraqi oil, end corruption, and bring all weapons under the exclusive control of the state”.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields
list 2 of 3  How an oil feud is deepening rift between Baghdad and Iraq’s Kurdish region
list 3 of 3  Democrats want to end Trump’s Iran war. But how different are they?
end of list
He said the United States wants a “united, prosperous, and strong Iraq that makes its own political decisions”. The endorsement comes as al-Zaidi, who has steered Iraq closer to Washington, risks antagonising both the Kurds and Iran, Agence France-Presse reported.
Haider al-Aboudi told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that Baghdad considers crude exports bypassing state marketer SOMO to be smuggling, since the proceeds do not reach the treasury. He said Iraq lost an estimated $100bn to smuggling through northern Iraq’s Kurdish region between 2008 and 2025.
Reuters said it was unclear how the government calculated the figure.
On Tuesday, al-Zaidi moved to place the Kurdish region’s border crossings and several oil fields under federal control, AFP reported. Iraq closed two crossings in the region on Thursday, one with Syria and one with Iran. Iraq’s highest court ruled on Wednesday that Baghdad can deploy federal forces along all international borders, including those of the Kurdish region of northern Iraq.
Oil Minister Basim Mohammed said: “The oilfields in the region and Basra belong to all Iraqis and remain under the Iraqi flag.” INA reported that he said Iraq would not be lenient towards “any drop of oil exported outside legal contexts”.
Men stand near tank trucks at a market for fuel oil and automotive fuel on March 17, 2026 in Erbil, Iraq [Photo by Sedat Suna/Getty Images]   Kurdish reaction
Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) spokesman Peshawa Hawramani said the region does not want clashes with Baghdad, but sees the central government’s actions as aimed at restricting the semi-autonomous region and violating its constitutional rights.

items.title: Serbia’s student-led movement nominates chemistry professor for presidency

original_payload.original_title: Serbia’s student-led movement nominates chemistry professor for presidency
original_payload.original_body:
Serbia’s student-backed movement, which won an October  election  after rallying against corruption, has named university professor Radomir Saicic as its presidential candidate in next month’s polls.
Saicic, who teaches chemistry at Belgrade University, is a member of the newly elected parliament as a representative of the Student List, which won 140 seats in the 250-member parliament.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Trump embraced Xi, then slapped new tariffs on China: What’s his game plan?
list 2 of 3  Eisenkot navigates tricky waters as he tests power-sharing with Netanyahu
list 3 of 3  Why did Georgian police clash with Turkish football fans over Palestine?
end of list
The role is largely ceremonial, but the president is responsible for nominating prime ministers and serves as commander-in-chief of the armed forces.
The December 27 presidential vote comes after Aleksandar Vucic – who dominated Serbian politics for 14 years – cut short his second presidential term to run for prime minister but was  soundly defeated  by the student-led movement in the parliamentary ballot.
Speaking at a televised news conference in Belgrade on Friday, Saicic said the movement must now prioritise strengthening the rule of law and fighting corruption.
“Now we have the opportunity to turn the freedom we fought for into lasting change,” he said.
“The assembly, the government and the courts must once again earn the trust of the people. The same applies to the institution of the president.”
Saicic pledged a “sovereign Serbia in which the constitution will be respected and in which every citizen will be able to live with dignity”.
original_payload.original_summary: Radomir Saicic, who teaches at Belgrade University, was among the first university professors to join the movement.

A landmark ruling by Canada’s Supreme Court has largely upheld Quebec’s secularism law, leaving in place a ban on public school teachers, police officers and some other public employees wearing religious symbols at work.
The ruling settles a years-long legal battle over a law that has forced some workers to choose between their careers and how they practise their faith.

items.title: ‘Playing with fire’: Trump faces GOP backlash over Nvidia CEO’s return

original_payload.original_title: ‘Playing with fire’: Trump faces GOP backlash over Nvidia CEO’s return
original_payload.original_body:
United States President Donald Trump’s involvement in getting NVIDIA CEO  Jensen Huang reinstated  has drawn little support from his own party with some Republican officials warning this could be a blow to the president’s popularity with his conservative base.
Earlier this week, the US president ignited a firestorm across Washington, DC, after he revealed he personally contacted NVIDIA’s board of directors and “convinced” its members to let Huang return.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Todd Blanche declines to confirm if Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was investigated
list 2 of 3  Asia’s markets dive as return of Nvidia’s Huang fails to quell AI doubts
list 3 of 3  ‘Second home’: Why Israel is celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
end of list
Trump said he spoke to the board “directly and indirectly” in the less than two weeks between Huang’s resignation and his reinstatement, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The move amounted to an extraordinary intervention by the US president, whose predecessors, both Democratic and Republican, have largely avoided personally involving themselves – or their administrations – in corporate matters.
“I felt very strongly about it,” Trump told CNBC on Monday about his decision to contact NVIDIA’s board. “And I felt more strongly as I saw what was happening with the … company, because that was, to me, a very important part of our country.”

The Professional Football Association’s Player of the Year was in the final year of his existing contract, which would have allowed him to speak with clubs outside the Premier League from January 1 about a move next summer.

Fernandes had revealed that  negotiations about a new contract had been put on hold , adding to speculation that he could seek a move away from a team that are currently in the league relegation zone.
United, however, are understood to have triggered a clause in the current deal to keep Fernandes at the Old Trafford club until the end of the 2027-2028 season.
Fernandes joined United in January 2020 from Sporting Lisbon, against whom he scored twice in the two sides’ midweek Champions League  2-2 draw .
The attacking midfielder quickly became the club’s most important player and last season performed a record number of assists in a Premier League season, helping secure the return to Europe’s elite competition for this campaign.
A team source said the move suited both parties and left the door open to future talks over a ⁠⁠new contract, although the immediate priority was improving results.

items.title: Erling Haaland ‘happy’ at Man City despite transfer talk, says Maresca

original_payload.original_title: Erling Haaland ‘happy’ at Man City despite transfer talk, says Maresca
original_payload.original_body:
Enzo Maresca insisted on Friday that Erling Haaland is “happy” at Manchester City after the striker expressed frustration over his side’s recent struggles.
Haaland gave a candid assessment of City’s malaise following Tuesday’s 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League, which came on the back of a Premier League draw at home with Fulham.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Pep Guardiola calls on world to ‘disobey horror’ over Gaza and praises BDS
list 2 of 4  Welcome to Manchester! Liverpool give Poch crash course in United’s woes
list 3 of 4  ‘Politics has poisoned cricket’: India-Pakistan fans fear for beloved sport
list 4 of 4  Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
end of list
After winning 10 of their first 11 matches in all competitions this season, Maresca’s men have won just two of their last seven.
With a crucial trip to Premier League leaders Arsenal looming on Sunday, Haaland’s criticism added to the growing sense that City’s season is in danger of spiralling out of control.
“We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way,” Haaland said.
“I have no idea what we were missing but you could feel it in the last few games that something was not clicking fully.”
Haaland has scored just once in his last five games for City and is without a league goal in his past three matches.
The Norway star’s body language has been noticeably angst-ridden in recent weeks, prompting suggestions that he is growing disillusioned with life at the Etihad Stadium.
City are also awaiting the result of their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, with the punishment potentially including a huge points deduction.
Despite City’s woes, Maresca is adamant Haaland remains committed to the cause regardless of speculation that he could seek a move at the end of the season.

items.title: RD Congo : le ton monte entre Kinshasa et l'armée ougandaise, déployée dans l'Est

original_payload.original_title: RD Congo : le ton monte entre Kinshasa et l'armée ougandaise, déployée dans l'Est
original_payload.original_body:
L'armée ougandaise a annoncé, vendredi 27 novembre, son intention de se retirer d'une importante localité congolaise et accusé certaines milices proches de Kinshasa de multiplier les exactions dans l'est de la  République démocratique du Congo  où ses troupes sont déployées en soutien de l'armée régulière congolaise.
Le ton est récemment monté entre les deux pays voisins, après la convocation d'un diplomate ougandais par Kinshasa et des déclarations ougandaises jugées hostiles.
L'est de la République démocratique du Congo est en proie à des conflits depuis plus de trente ans, auxquels le  Rwanda  et l' Ouganda  ont souvent participé de manière directe ou en soutenant des groupes armés locaux.
Depuis 2021, les forces armées ougandaises (UPDF) sont déployées dans les provinces de l'Ituri (nord-est) et du  Nord-Kivu  (est) frontalières de l'Ouganda, officiellement pour appuyer l'armée congolaises contre les rebelles ADF (Allied Democratic Forces) qui ont fait allégeance à l' organisation État islamique  et y commettent des massacres à répétition.
Mardi, les autorités de Kinshasa ont annoncé avoir convoqué le chef de mission de l'ambassade ougandaise après que le chef d'état-major de l'armée ougandaise – et fils du président  Yoweri Museveni  – a notamment menacé sur X de prendre le contrôle de Walikale, une cité minière stratégique du Nord-Kivu.
Vers un retrait des forces ougandaises de Lubero
Vendredi, le porte-parole de l'armée ougandaise a déclaré sur X que les forces ougandaises allaient "prochainement retirer leurs troupes" de Lubero, une agglomération située dans la province du Nord-Kivu où un déploiement de militaires ougandais en janvier 2025 avait freiné une offensive du groupe armé  M23   soutenu par le Rwanda .
À lire aussi  RD Congo : quel impact peut avoir l'alliance entre Joseph Kabila et l'AFC/M23 ?
Dans un second message, ce porte-parole a accusé des milices dont certaines "apparemment" alliées à Kinshasa de multiplier "les attaques contre des communautés vulnérables, massacrant des femmes et des enfants, notamment au sein des communautés" locales Hema et Tutsi.
"En vertu du droit international humanitaire, les UPDF conservent la responsabilité d'assurer la protection de ces communautés vulnérables et continueront à le faire chaque fois que cela sera possible", a-t-il ajouté.
Des combats intenses opposent depuis samedi dans la province de l'Ituri les forces de Kinshasa à la Convention pour la révolution populaire (CRP), groupe armé souvent assimilé à la communauté Hema et formé par  Thomas Lubanga , chef de guerre congolais  condamné par la Cour pénale internationale  et réputé proche de l'Ouganda, selon des sources locales.
Avec AFP
original_payload.original_summary: L'armée ougandaise a déclaré vendredi qu'elle prévoyait de se retirer de la ville de Lubero, dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo, et a accusé des milices proches de Kinshasa de multiplier les exactions dans la région.

items.title: Au Sénégal, Ousmane Sonko demande à Bassirou Diomaye Faye de dissoudre l'Assemblée

original_payload.original_title: Au Sénégal, Ousmane Sonko demande à Bassirou Diomaye Faye de dissoudre l'Assemblée
original_payload.original_body:
Le chef de la majorité parlementaire  Ousmane Sonko , en crise ouverte avec le président sénégalais  Bassirou Diomaye Faye  depuis des mois, a appelé jeudi 26 novembre à dissoudre l'Assemblée nationale et à organiser des élections législatives anticipées en 2027, dans un message vidéo adressé à ses partisans.
Le  Sénégal  vit au rythme d'un conflit ouvert entre Ousmane Sonko, président de l'Assemblée, et son ex-allié Bassirou Diomaye Faye qui l'avait nommé Premier ministre en avril 2024 avant de le limoger en mai.
Depuis octobre, le pays se trouve dans une impasse budgétaire avec un  rejet par le parti Pastef  (Parti africain pour la solidarité, le travail, l'éthique et la fraternité),  également dirigé par Ousmane Sonko , de tous les textes sur les finances publiques soumis par l'exécutif.
À lire aussi  Sénégal : Bassirou Diomaye Faye radié du Pastef, signe de la "séparation définitive" avec Sonko
Mais, en se fondant sur l'article 68 de la Constitution, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a décidé le 19 novembre de contourner l'Assemblée nationale en faisant passer par décret le budget rectificatif 2026, jugé crucial pour ce pays surendetté et  en négociations avec le Fonds monétaire international  (FMI) pour une aide financière.
Le  FMI  a en effet annoncé en septembre un accord préliminaire avec Dakar sur un nouveau programme d'aide de 2,2 milliards de dollars (1,93 milliard d'euros) sur 36 mois. Mais le Fonds n'a pas encore annoncé l'approbation de l'accord par son conseil d'administration.
À voir aussi  Sénégal : l’accord avec le FMI, une bouffée d’oxygène face à la cherté de la vie ?
"Qu'il s'arme de courage"
"Si ça ne dépendait que de moi, le 2 décembre, je signerais le décret de dissolution de l'Assemblée nationale. Dans les trois mois qui vont suivre (cette dissolution), nous allons retourner (aux urnes) et les Sénégalais décideront", a déclaré Ousmane Sonko dans une vidéo adressée à ses partisans et postée jeudi soir sur son compte Facebook.
Le chef de l'État peut légalement dissoudre l'Assemblée à partir du 2 décembre, deux ans après son installation le 2 décembre 2024, et organiser des législatives anticipées dans les 60 à 90 jours.
Des membres de "la famille politique du président (Faye) réclament aussi la dissolution, donc le débat est clos. Mais je constate que le président a peur d'aller aux élections. Qu'il s'arme de courage pour qu'on aille solliciter les suffrages des Sénégalais. C'est mieux que gouverner par décret (présidentiel), en violation de la Constitution", a poursuivi Ousmane Sonko.
Le Pastef contrôle 130 des 165 sièges à l'Assemblée nationale.
Bassirou Diomaye Faye – dont le parti "Kiiraay – Les Patriotes républicains" (dont le nom signifie "protection" ou "bouclier" en langue wolof) a été lancé en juillet dernier – ne dispose officiellement pas de députés.
Avec AFP

items.title: Burundi bars main opposition leader from next year's presidential election

original_payload.original_title: Burundi bars main opposition leader from next year's presidential election
original_payload.original_body:
Burundi
Burundi's electoral commission on Friday rejected an application from the country's main opposition leader to contest in the presidential polls next year. President Evariste Ndayishimiye will seek a second term in the May 3 general elections for the ruling CNDD-FDD party, which has been in power since 2005 and is widely considered the favourite. Agathon Rwasa, an ex-militia leader who fought in the country's civil war, lost to Ndayishimiye in 2020's polls, which the opposition labelled an "electoral charade".
The electoral commission said Rwasa had made a "false declaration" in his application, as he had registered as an independent candidate despite remaining a member of a political party. "Consequently, the Independent National Electoral Commission rejects his candidacy," according to an official document seen by AFP. The commission approved seven out of 10 applicants, and those rejected have two days to challenge the decision before the Constitutional Court.
The final list of candidates will be published on December 6. Rwasa's disqualification came as "no surprise" to prominent exiled civil society activist Pacifique Nininahazwe. "It concludes a process of political elimination initiated by the regime of Évariste Ndayishimiye... to neutralise his primary rival," he told AFP. Burundi is one of the world's poorest countries and has a history of deadly political crises and a civil war that killed around 300,000 people between 1993 and 2005. Earlier this month, Ndayishimiye submitted his candidacy papers, paying a deposit of 100 million Burundian francs ($33,000).
original_payload.original_summary: Burundi's main opposition leader has been barred from contesting next year's presidential election, raising fresh concerns over political competition in the country.

items.title: Canal+ targets half of African TV households as it expands local content production

original_payload.original_title: Canal+ targets half of African TV households as it expands local content production
original_payload.original_body:
Media
French media group Canal+ is targeting subscriptions in at least half of African households with access to television, as it expands its operations following its acquisition of South African pay-TV giant MultiChoice .
The ambition comes as the company looks to tap into Africa's growing population, expanding electricity access and demand for locally produced entertainment.
Speaking at the launch of Canal+'s training academy in Johannesburg, David Mignot, CEO of Canal+ Africa and MultiChoice, said African productions remain central to the group's strategy, with thousands of hours of content produced annually in local languages.
original_payload.original_summary: With competition from international streaming platforms intensifying, Canal+ is betting that locally produced stories, accessible distribution and investment in African creative talent will help secure its position in the continent's rapidly evolving media market.

items.title: Moroccans turn to prayer as historic drought deepens across the country

original_payload.original_title: Moroccans turn to prayer as historic drought deepens across the country
original_payload.original_body:
Morocco
Moroccans have gathered for traditional prayers for rain as the country continues to battle one of its worst droughts in decades.
In the city of Salé, worshippers joined Quranic schoolchildren on Friday for Salat al-Istisqa, the Islamic prayer for rain, following a call by King Mohammed VI.
The participants took to the streets carrying small wooden tablets inscribed with Quranic verses before gathering inside a mosque, where an imam led the prayer and delivered a sermon.
original_payload.original_summary: With drought tightening its grip, Moroccans are turning to prayer for relief from the skies.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau's military government defends postponement of elections

original_payload.original_title: Guinea-Bissau's military government defends postponement of elections
original_payload.original_body:
Guinea-Bissau
Guinea-Bissau has defended its decision to postpone next month’s planned presidential and legislative elections until 2028.
Its military leaders on Thursday said conditions were not in place to hold the polls and stick to the one-year transition to civilian rule promised after last year’s coup.
Transitional president, General Horta N'Tam, said government of the country has been assured at all levels in the current “special context”.

items.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from eastern DR Congo town amid diplomatic spat

original_payload.original_title: Uganda to withdraw troops from eastern DR Congo town amid diplomatic spat
original_payload.original_body:
Uganda
Uganda's army said on Friday it planned to withdraw from a key DR Congo town and accused militias apparently allied to the Congolese government of stepping up attacks in the strife-torn eastern region.
The Ugandan announcement comes days after the DRC said   it had summoned the Ugandan embassy's head of mission   over remarks by the country's army chief.
The mineral-rich eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has been wracked by violence for more than 30 years, often drawing in its neighbours Uganda and Rwanda directly or through support for local armed groups.

items.title: China and Belt and Road partners step up cooperation on green energy

original_payload.original_title: China and Belt and Road partners step up cooperation on green energy
original_payload.original_body:
China
Energy ministers from Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) participating countries have stressed the importance of cooperation in advancing green transition and safeguarding energy security across the globe.
These priorities took center stage as the Fourth Belt and Road Energy Ministerial Conference wrapped up in east China's Qingdao on Friday. Held under the theme "Sharing innovation outcomes, advancing energy transition, building a secure future together," the two-day event brought officials together to translate those goals into action.
Discussions centered on innovation-driven energy transition, energy security and system resilience, and coordinated efforts toward a green, low-carbon transition across industrial and supply chains. During the conference, Wang Hongzhi, administrator of the National Energy Administration of China, said China is accelerating its new energy system. By 2030, China aims for a cleaner, low-carbon system, with a better energy mix, stronger resilience and more innovation.
original_payload.original_summary: Energy cooperation is taking centre stage as Belt and Road countries push for a greener, more secure global energy future. Ministers wrapped up the Fourth Belt and Road Energy Ministerial Conference in Qingdao, eastern China.

items.title: Europe's biggest museum complex about to open in the Belgian capital

original_payload.original_title: Europe's biggest museum complex about to open in the Belgian capital
original_payload.original_body:
Belgium
Built inside a former Citroën showroom in the Belgian capital, Brussels, the Kanal-Centre Pompidou museum is opening its doors to the public on Saturday.
The building on the banks of a canal has been restored with three new ones added to the existing structure, making it the biggest museum complex in Europe.
Its 40,000 square metres features gallery spaces, two auditoria, a library, restaurants, a rooftop bar, and a research centre.

items.title: Putin unveils new nuclear-powered submarine, promises five more by 2030

original_payload.original_title: Putin unveils new nuclear-powered submarine, promises five more by 2030
original_payload.original_body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine and said Russia would add five more to the country’s fleet by 2030, according to footage released by the Kremlin.
At the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk, Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm submarine, marking its formal transfer to the navy.
“Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance,” he said.
Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia’s nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack.
Putin said the navy would receive five more by 2030, including three vessels from the Yasen-M class, the same class as the Perm.

items.title: EFCC arraigns woman over N62.5m Hajj visa fraud in Kwara

original_payload.original_title: EFCC arraigns woman over N62.5m Hajj visa fraud in Kwara
original_payload.original_body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has arraigned a woman, Hauwa Mohammed Abdulkadir, before the Kwara State High Court in Ilorin over an alleged N62.5 million fraud involving intending Muslim pilgrims travelling to Saudi Arabia for the 2026 Hajj.
Abdulkadir was arraigned on Thursday, November 26, 2026, before Justice Haleema Saleeman on a seven-count charge bordering on obtaining money by false pretence, contrary to Section 1(1)(a) and punishable under Section 1(3) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006.
According to the EFCC on X on Friday, the defendant allegedly presented herself as a travel agent with the capacity to process Saudi Arabian visas and flight tickets for intending pilgrims.
The commission alleged that she collected various sums of money from several victims under the pretence of securing the necessary travel documents for their pilgrimage.

items.title: ITF targets unemployment through skills acquisition

original_payload.original_title: ITF targets unemployment through skills acquisition
original_payload.original_body:
The Industrial Training Fund has pledged to strengthen its vocational and technical training programmes and deepen collaboration with the private sector following its emergence as the Most Responsive Agency at the 2026 Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association Employers’ Excellence Awards.
The recognition comes amid growing concerns over unemployment and the gap between the skills possessed by job seekers and those required by employers, with technical and vocational education increasingly seen as critical to improving workforce productivity.
The award, organised by NECA, recognises the ITF’s contributions to workforce development, particularly through its skills acquisition and vocational training interventions.
In a statement issued by the agency on Friday after the ceremony, the Director-General of the ITF, Afiz Ogun, expressed appreciation to NECA for recognising the agency’s efforts, describing the award as an encouragement to do more in developing the country’s human capital.

items.title: Atiku challenges FG over rice import policy, farmers’ support

original_payload.original_title: Atiku challenges FG over rice import policy, farmers’ support
original_payload.original_body:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the President Bola Tinubu-led government of undermining Nigeria’s rice industry through policies that allegedly favour imports over local production, demanding an explanation for a reported concession granted to an importer to bring in 150,000 metric tonnes of brown rice.
Atiku, who made the allegations in a statement issued on Friday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, also challenged the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council to provide evidence of its claim that the Federal Government had committed N450bn to support rice farmers and stabilise the market.
The former vice president questioned the administration’s claim that N250bn had been committed to smallholder farmer support, while another N200bn was earmarked for a guaranteed minimum price programme.
He argued that announcing financial commitments without disclosing actual disbursements, beneficiaries and measurable outcomes amounted to little more than political propaganda.

Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has alleged that former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, is contesting the 2027 presidential election mainly to remain in the news rather than because he expects to win.
Bwala also claimed that Obi’s running mate, former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, joined him because of his alleged ambition to contest the presidency in 2031.

Obi made the call on Friday while addressing supporters at the Primetime Event Centre along the Port Harcourt-Aba Expressway in Aba, where he accused the Tinubu administration of failing to deliver on its campaign promises and worsening poverty.
He said the government he hopes to form with Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso would prioritise national unity, economic growth and the development of critical sectors, including power, education and healthcare.

items.title: Uganda launches Africa’s first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial

original_payload.original_title: Uganda launches Africa’s first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial
original_payload.original_body:
Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO).
Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection.
But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic.

items.title: Ebola: Canada extends visa restrictions on three African countries by 90 days

original_payload.original_title: Ebola: Canada extends visa restrictions on three African countries by 90 days
original_payload.original_body:
Canada has extended its temporary immigration restrictions on residents of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda and South Sudan for another 90 days, suspending the use of previously approved visas and travel documents until February 25, 2027, over the Ebola outbreak.
Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada announced the extension on Friday, saying the measures were being maintained as the government continued to monitor the outbreak in the DRC and developments in neighbouring countries.
In the announcement published on its website, the Canadian government said, “Protecting the health and safety of Canadians remains a top priority.”
It added that it was “taking a precautionary, proactive approach to help prevent Ebola disease from entering Canada.”

items.title: WHO seeks faster Ebola vaccine trials as DRC deaths hit 5,900

original_payload.original_title: WHO seeks faster Ebola vaccine trials as DRC deaths hit 5,900
original_payload.original_body:
The World Health Organisation has called for faster clinical trials of potential Ebola vaccines and treatments, as the outbreak of the Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed about 5,900 people and security challenges continue to hamper efforts to contain its spread.
The global health agency said more than 12,000 cases and 5,900 deaths had been reported in the DRC as of November 24, while at least 94 attacks on healthcare had been recorded since the outbreak was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern six months ago.
The WHO made the recommendations in an update issued on Friday, following the third meeting of its Emergency Committee on November 17.
It called for accelerated clinical trials of candidate vaccines and treatments, while stressing that scientific, ethical and safety standards must be maintained. The committee also highlighted the importance of involving local communities and providing transparent information about the trials.

items.title: Zelensky faults Trump for calling Putin his ‘friend’

original_payload.original_title: Zelensky faults Trump for calling Putin his ‘friend’
original_payload.original_body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has criticised United States President Donald Trump for describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as his “friend”, likening the Russian leader to Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler.
Zelensky made the remarks in an interview with the BBC aired on Friday, saying Putin could not be regarded as a friend because of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
“Of course it’s up to the president of the United States, but … it’s strange,” Zelensky said.
“He is an aggressor, and a killer… He can’t be a friend. Just cannot be.”

original_payload.original_title: Musiala joins Kane on Bayern’s growing injury list
original_payload.original_body:

Le tribunal régional de Harare a reporté au lundi 30 novembre sa décision sur la demande de remise en liberté sous caution de Uebert Angel. Le magistrat Francis Mapfumo a mis son jugement en délibéré jeudi 26 novembre, maintenant le fondateur de Spirit Embassy en détention pendant le week-end.
Le prédicateur zimbabwéen, dont le nom civil est Uebert Mudzanire, fait l’objet d’une poursuite pour agression sexuelle aggravée. Les faits allégués remonteraient à février 2025 et concerneraient une femme de 40 ans venue solliciter une aide financière auprès de son église.
Selon l’accusation, Uebert Angel aurait remis 1 000 dollars à la plaignante avant de l’agresser dans son bureau. Ces éléments constituent la version présentée au tribunal par le parquet et n’ont pas encore fait l’objet d’un jugement au fond.
Le ministère public s’oppose à sa libération, invoquant un risque de fuite et de pression sur les témoins. Les procureurs ont notamment cité ses deux passeports, des divergences entre les adresses qui y figurent et son influence comme responsable religieux et ambassadeur itinérant du Zimbabwe.
La défense affirme au contraire que son client dispose d’un domicile fixe, possède plusieurs biens dans le pays et entretient des liens familiaux solides au Zimbabwe. Elle a proposé une caution de 5 000 dollars, le dépôt de ses deux passeports, la remise d’un titre de propriété et un pointage hebdomadaire au commissariat de Highlands.
Uebert Angel a été arrêté dimanche 22 novembre pendant un culte à Harare. Sa demande de remise en liberté a été examinée pendant plusieurs audiences avant la clôture des débats jeudi. Le tribunal doit annoncer sa décision lundi à 14 h 15.

Le Conseil national de transition (CNT) du Mali a adopté jeudi 26 novembre le projet de loi sur la deuxième phase du programme d’irrigation du Bani et de Sélingué (PDI-BS II). Le texte a recueilli les 116 voix des membres présents. Les interventions prévues à Sélingué, dans le Moyen-Bani et à Djenné portent sur 59 445 hectares, répartis entre cultures et pâturages.
La plus grande part concerne les plaines dont l’inondation sera contrôlée, avec 44 000 hectares. Le programme prévoit également 10 416 hectares où les apports d’eau pourront être entièrement maîtrisés, 4 879 hectares de pâturages inondables et 150 hectares consacrés au maraîchage. Pour faciliter l’acheminement des récoltes, 391 kilomètres de pistes rurales sont prévus, dont 12 kilomètres bitumés.
Le dispositif est destiné à soutenir la riziculture, les cultures légumières, l’élevage et la pêche. Le programme initial, institué par la loi du 12 février 2016, avait subi des interruptions de travaux liées aux crises politique et sécuritaire. Le  Conseil des ministres du 9 octobre 2026  avait retenu une durée de cinq ans pour la deuxième phase afin de poursuivre les aménagements.
Des marchés de travaux déjà conclus dans le Moyen-Bani
Le vote intervient une semaine après la réunion du comité de pilotage du programme. Le 19 novembre, le ministre de l’Agriculture, Ibrahima Samaké, avait fait état d’un financement de 30 milliards de FCFA avec le concours de la Banque ouest-africaine de développement (BOAD) pour les investissements dans le Moyen-Bani.
Selon le bilan présenté par le ministre, les contrats portent notamment sur les aménagements de Sirimanso (2 000 hectares) et de Woloni (2 300 hectares), des stations de pompage et 40 kilomètres de pistes. La commission du développement rural du CNT a demandé au gouvernement de veiller à la sécurité des zones d’intervention, au suivi de la qualité des ouvrages et à la recherche de financements supplémentaires.

Le Real Madrid a  officialisé vendredi  la prolongation de Brahim Díaz jusqu’au 30 juin 2031. L’international marocain, dont le précédent contrat devait s’achever en 2027, s’engage ainsi pour quatre saisons supplémentaires avec le club espagnol.

Cette prolongation conforte également la place du Marocain dans un secteur offensif très concurrentiel. Sa capacité à évoluer dans l’axe comme sur les côtés lui a permis de conserver un rôle régulier depuis son retour d’Italie.
Le nouveau contrat intervient au terme d’une année marquée par son importance croissante avec la sélection marocaine. Brahim Díaz totalise 36 sélections et 15 buts avec les Lions de l’Atlas.

SOMMAIRE
Une mise en garde antérieure aux arrestations
La police togolaise a rendu publiques le 26 novembre les premières conclusions de son enquête sur Curiosity Brave Compass (CBC). Plusieurs responsables présumés de cette plateforme de placement financier ont été interpellés. Selon la police, la structure exerçait sans agrément au Togo et présentait les caractéristiques d’un système de Ponzi.
Les premières arrestations remontent au 17 novembre, dans le quartier d’Adidoadin à Lomé. La Direction centrale de la police judiciaire a ensuite mené des opérations à Sagbado, à Kégué et à Kara. Sept autres personnes soupçonnées de participer aux activités de CBC ont été arrêtées. Des téléphones et des ordinateurs ont été saisis et plusieurs locaux placés sous scellés.
La plateforme promettait à ses adhérents des revenus quotidiens en contrepartie de tâches publicitaires sur Internet. Les trois formules proposées représentaient des mises allant de 9 600 à 96 000 FCFA. Dans chaque cas, le rendement annoncé atteignait plus de 3 % du capital par jour. La police estime que les sommes versées aux premiers adhérents provenaient des apports des suivants plutôt que de recettes tirées d’une activité économique réelle.
Une mise en garde antérieure aux arrestations
Le CERT.tg, chargé de la réponse aux incidents de cybersécurité au Togo, avait déjà cité CBCApp dans une  alerte publiée le 6 septembre 2026 . Celle-ci concernait plusieurs plateformes d’investissement et de jeux d’argent. Le dispositif de prévention concerne aussi la protection des données personnelles transmises lors de l’inscription à ces services. Les risques liés aux transactions numériques touchent également les pays voisins, comme le montrent les  pertes recensées au Burkina Faso en octobre .
Le Mouvement Martin Luther King (MMLK) a demandé le 25 novembre la suspension temporaire des systèmes de placement de fonds et de marketing de réseau. L’organisation togolaise réclame également un examen des agréments. Elle demande aussi un accompagnement des personnes ayant perdu leurs économies.
Les investigations judiciaires se poursuivent sur les mouvements de fonds et d’éventuels faits de blanchiment. Selon la police, certains responsables présumés restent recherchés au Togo et à l’étranger.

items.title: PM Abiy Pledges Continued Abay River Development, Regional Cooperation

original_payload.original_title: PM Abiy Pledges Continued Abay River Development, Regional Cooperation
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)— Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has reaffirmed Ethiopia’s sovereign right to develop and utilize the Abay River without external authorization, while pledging to pursue shared regional development through cooperation with downstream countries.
The Prime Minister made the remarks while responding to Members of the House of Peoples’ Representatives’ questions on regional diplomacy and water resources during the fourth regular session of the first year of the house.
Describing the Abay as a divine gift to Ethiopia, PM Abiy stressed that harnessing the river’s potential is essential to overcoming poverty, expanding energy production, strengthening food security, and improving the livelihoods of citizens.
“Abay is a potent remedy given to us by the grace of God, and we will use it. We do not need anyone’s permission for that,” he told parliamentarians.
He said Ethiopia’s development ambitions are inseparable from its sovereign right to utilize its natural resources. The PM added  that the country’s approach to the river is grounded in shared responsibility rather than unilateral exploitation.
“Abay does not belong to us alone; it is also the rightful share of our neighbors, which we respect and protect for them,” the Prime Minister said.
PM Abiy emphasized that Ethiopia has no intention of monopolizing the river and remains committed to cooperation with downstream countries, particularly Egypt and Sudan, to advance equitable and responsible water utilization.
“We have no desire to use it exclusively; we will use it lawfully, assist, and cooperate,” he stated.
The Prime Minister also welcomed reports of agricultural expansion in Egypt, expressing Ethiopia’s desire to see Egyptian agriculture flourish alongside Ethiopia’s own efforts to expand energy production.
He said the two countries’ development aspirations could advance together through cooperation.
Addressing environmental concerns and the long-term sustainability of the river, the Premier highlighted the role of Ethiopia’s Green Legacy Initiative, particularly tree planting, reforestation, and soil conservation, in protecting the Abay basin.
“We plant trees so that the Abay does not diminish; and we responsibly uphold our neighbors' rightful share,” he said.
He underscored the importance of protecting the river’s source and addressing environmental pressures, including deforestation, soil erosion, and siltation, as part of responsible water-resource management.
PM Abiy also challenged the zero-sum narrative surrounding the Abay, arguing that Ethiopia’s development should not be viewed as coming at the expense of downstream countries.
He stressed that the expansion of Ethiopia’s energy capacity and agricultural development in neighboring countries could complement one another through dialogue and cooperation.
Beyond the Abay basin, the Prime Minister highlighted Ethiopia’s role as a source of freshwater for neighboring countries, including Eritrea, Somalia, Kenya, Sudan, and Djibouti, stressing that Ethiopia has no intention of obstructing shared water resources.
He further called for educational and public narratives that promote brotherhood and cooperation among the peoples of Ethiopia, Egypt, Sudan, Djibouti, and Eritrea rather than hostility.
Emphasizing the regional benefits of Ethiopia’s prosperity and stability, Prime Minister Abiy likened a prosperous Ethiopia to a shade-giving sycamore tree beside a spring, offering vitality and relief to neighboring countries.
He said the central challenge was to transform Ethiopia’s abundant natural resources into tangible economic benefits while strengthening good-neighborly relations and advancing mutually beneficial development across the region.

items.title: Ethiopia Promotes Investment Opportunities to Turkish Business Community

original_payload.original_title: Ethiopia Promotes Investment Opportunities to Turkish Business Community
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)— Ethiopia has stepped up efforts to attract Turkish investment and expand economic cooperation, as its Embassy in Ankara convened a business and investment forum in Eskişehir, Türkiye, bringing together more than 70 business representatives.
Held on 26 November 2026, the forum was organized to showcase Ethiopia’s investment potential and explore opportunities for stronger trade and business partnerships between the two countries.
According to Ethiopia’s Embassy in Ankara, participants represented a range of sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, energy, information and communication technology (ICT), and hospitality.
Opening the forum, Ethiopian Ambassador to Türkiye Shimelis Adugna highlighted Ethiopia’s strategic location, large domestic market, ongoing economic reforms, and efforts to create a favorable environment for foreign direct investment.
He called on Turkish businesses to explore the wide-ranging investment opportunities across key sectors of Ethiopia’s economy.
The Chairman of the Eskişehir Chamber of Commerce, in turn, encouraged chamber members to familiarize themselves with Ethiopia’s economic potential and emerging investment opportunities.
He also expressed his intention to lead a business delegation comprising interested member companies to Ethiopia in the near future to explore concrete trade and investment prospects.
Such a visit, he noted, would help strengthen business-to-business ties and advance economic cooperation between the two countries.

items.title: CPHIA 2026 Closes with Call for African Ownership of Health Security

original_payload.original_title: CPHIA 2026 Closes with Call for African Ownership of Health Security
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)—            The five-day 2026 Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA) concluded in Addis Ababa today with a strong call for African countries to take greater ownership of their health security through increased domestic investment, resilient health systems, and stronger continental cooperation.
Closing the conference, Ethiopia’s Health Minister, Dr. Mekdes Daba, urged African governments to translate the commitments made during the gathering into tangible action through national budgets, legislation, and improved frontline healthcare delivery.
The conference brought together more than 50,000 registered participants and featured over 90 sessions, attracting heads of state, ministers, scientists, health professionals, researchers, and private sector leaders.
Highlighting Ethiopia’s efforts to strengthen domestic health financing, Dr. Mekdes said the government is funding its health extension workers entirely through local resources.
She noted that Ethiopia aims to increase the government’s share of health financing to 53 percent by 2030 while reducing out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure to 20 percent.
The minister called on African countries to prioritize pandemic preparedness, primary healthcare, predictable domestic financing, and local pharmaceutical manufacturing, including the production of African-made vaccines and other essential medical products.
She also stressed the importance of stronger partnerships with the private sector, civil society, researchers, and young people in building sustainable health systems and advancing African-led solutions.
Outlining the next steps, Dr. Mekdes identified three key actions: reviewing conference priorities and incorporating them into national plans and budgets within 90 days; establishing a permanent multi-stakeholder platform; and assessing progress at the next CPHIA.
Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya described CPHIA 2026 as a milestone in continental public health cooperation, declaring that “CPHIA is not just a conference; CPHIA is a movement” toward African health sovereignty.
He said discussions had highlighted Africa’s growing capacity in pandemic preparedness, local manufacturing, and domestic health financing, while stressing the need for countries to learn from one another and deepen regional cooperation.
Dr. Kaseya also called for more equitable partnerships with development partners, emphasizing that African countries must assume greater responsibility for their health security through domestic investment, good governance, and accountability.
He identified the African Pooled Procurement Mechanism and the African Medicines Agency as important instruments for reducing dependence on external suppliers and strengthening pharmaceutical production across the continent.
He reaffirmed Africa CDC’s commitment to building a continental community that connects countries, facilitates experience-sharing, coordinates health priorities, and advances collective ownership of Africa’s health security.
For his part, Addis Ababa Deputy Mayor Samuel Molalign called for stronger cooperation in developing urban health solutions, highlighting the capital’s use of artificial intelligence and digital health technologies to improve patient record management, identify health risks early, and deliver more efficient healthcare services.
He said Addis Ababa remained open to piloting innovative urban health initiatives in collaboration with partners.
Samuel also encouraged participants to share Ethiopia’s development and healthcare achievements in their respective countries and serve as ambassadors for Addis Ababa and Ethiopia.
During the five-day conference, two continental health roadmaps were also launched.
The first seeks to improve maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health by 2030 and is championed by Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan. The second focuses on advancing African-led artificial intelligence and digital health solutions and is championed by Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

items.title: Guba-launched Mega Projects Poised to Shape Ethiopia’s Medemer Vision, Say MPs

original_payload.original_title: Guba-launched Mega Projects Poised to Shape Ethiopia’s Medemer Vision, Say MPs
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)—Ethiopia’s Guba-launched mega-development projects, valued at more than 30 billion USD, hold immense potential to accelerate economic transformation and shape the country’s emerging Medemer civilization, members of the House of Peoples’ Representatives told ENA.
The lawmakers described the strategic projects as major engines of national growth, saying their successful completion would expand economic opportunities, enhance citizens’ livelihoods and lay a stronger foundation for Ethiopia’s long-term prosperity.
Their remarks follow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s address to the House during the fourth regular session of the first working year of the seventh parliament, where he outlined the progress, strategic significance and national aspirations underpinning the Guba-launched initiatives.
Guided by the vision of “A Great Country, A Great People, A Grand Vision,” the projects demonstrate Ethiopia’s capacity to undertake ambitious development initiatives while pursuing greater economic self-reliance, the Prime Minister explained.
The strategic portfolio encompasses the Bishoftu International Airport, the Ogaden natural gas project, the 1.5-million-housing development program, nuclear energy initiatives and the Gode soil fertilizer factory.
Providing updates on their implementation, PM Abiy disclosed that natural gas from the Ogaden project in the Somali Region is already being used as an input by domestic ceramics factories and for powering Addis Ababa’s city buses, illustrating its contribution to the country's industrial and transport sectors.
He also said preparations for the Bishoftu International Airport are advancing with the support of modern artificial intelligence technologies.
Initial site selection has been completed, while the tender process for runway construction is underway.
The Gode fertilizer factory is also progressing under close supervision, with the development including nearly 18,000 residential units for workers. Meanwhile, the 1.5-million-housing program is incorporating modern construction approaches designed to take citizens’ purchasing power into account.
Approached by ENA, MP Addis Alemayehu said the pace of implementation of the mega-projects within a relatively short period was encouraging. She described  them as a manifestation of the vision to hand over a more prosperous Ethiopia to future generations.
MP Abiyot Delelegn, for her part, highlighted the projects’ round-the-clock construction activities as evidence of an emerging work culture focused on translating national ambitions into tangible results.
She said the initiatives have considerable potential to shape Ethiopia’s new Medemer civilization by strengthening the country's development capacity and expanding opportunities for its people.
Another MP, Samson Wondmeneh, said the government's vision of positioning Ethiopia as an African beacon of prosperity is being pursued through strategic development planning and major national investments.
The lawmaker further reaffirmed their commitment to discharging their parliamentary oversight, support and regulatory responsibilities to ensure the projects are completed within their stipulated timelines and required quality standards and become operational.
They emphasized that the successful realization of these strategic investments would be instrumental in advancing Ethiopia’s economic transformation and building a foundation for sustainable prosperity for generations to come.

items.title: Prime Minister Abiy Reaffirms Ethiopia’s Readiness to Help Restore Peace in Sudan

original_payload.original_title: Prime Minister Abiy Reaffirms Ethiopia’s Readiness to Help Restore Peace in Sudan
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)— Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has reaffirmed Ethiopia’s readiness to commit its resources to restoring peace and stability in war-torn Sudan.
The Prime Minister also called on Eritrea to end its alleged support for forces hostile to Ethiopia and embrace peaceful coexistence and mutual development.
Addressing the House of Peoples’ Representatives on Thursday, the Prime Minister outlined Ethiopia’s foreign policy priorities toward neighboring countries, underscoring the country’s commitment to regional peace, cooperation and shared prosperity.
On Sudan, Prime Minister Abiy reiterated Ethiopia’s longstanding commitment to its neighbor’s stability, emphasizing the deep historical, social and brotherly ties between the two countries.
“Sudan’s peace is our peace,” he told lawmakers, reaffirming Ethiopia’s willingness to contribute whatever it can to help the country overcome its devastating conflict.
“If Ethiopia can contribute in any way to restoring Sudan to where it was, we are ready to spend our time and our money,” he said, urging the warring parties to give the proposed peace initiative a chance, noting that dialogue could produce meaningful results.
The Prime Minister’s remarks build on his recent initiative inviting Sudanese military, political and civilian stakeholders to an inclusive national dialogue hosted and facilitated by Ethiopia.
In a statement issued in Arabic, PM Abiy described the initiative as a sincere effort to help Sudan overcome its prolonged conflict through an inclusive, Sudanese-led political process.
“At this critical historical juncture, the Ethiopian government is putting forward a sincere and genuine initiative calling on all Sudanese parties, across their military, political, and civilian components, to participate in a comprehensive and open Sudanese dialogue to be hosted and facilitated by Ethiopia,” he stated.
Turning to Eritrea, the Prime Minister detailed Ethiopia’s extensive diplomatic and economic efforts to build constructive relations following the rapprochement between the two countries.
The Premier also expressing disappointment over Eritrean regime’s rejection of opportunities for cooperation.
He recalled that Ethiopia had played an active role in helping Eritrea reconnect with regional neighbors after years of diplomatic isolation, including providing Ethiopian aircraft to facilitate engagements with countries with which Eritrean officials had limited contact.
Beyond diplomatic engagement, Ethiopia had also proposed practical economic cooperation, including electricity supplies at domestic Ethiopian rates and joint development of roads and ports to address infrastructure and energy constraints.
However, he said, the Eritrean government rejected these proposals, arguing that its lack of a development-oriented vision had undermined opportunities for bilateral cooperation.
“The reason is that while the Eritrean government is a government for the time being, words like development and growth do not exist in its vocabulary,” PM Abiy said.
The Prime Minister also recalled the initial goodwill demonstrated by Eritrea following the attack on Ethiopia’s Northern Command but said relations subsequently deteriorated after Eritrean forces entered the Tigray region during the conflict.
He accused the forces of involvement in killings, looting and the destruction of infrastructure, adding that relations further soured following the signing of the Pretoria Peace Agreement.
Against this backdrop, Prime Minister Abiy called on Eritrea to make a clear choice between confrontation and cooperation, outlining two essential expectations for the future of bilateral relations: ending support for forces hostile to Ethiopia and pursuing mutually beneficial development.
He urged Asmara to immediately stop arming Ethiopia’s adversaries, end its alleged role as a weapons supply channel and cease cooperation with forces undermining peace and stability.

items.title: Ethiopia’s ICAO Council Election Marks Diplomatic Milestone, Strengthens Africa’s Voice in Global Aviation

original_payload.original_title: Ethiopia’s ICAO Council Election Marks Diplomatic Milestone, Strengthens Africa’s Voice in Global Aviation
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)— Ethiopia’s election to the Governing Council of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), securing 133 votes, marks a significant diplomatic milestone that strengthens the country’s role in global aviation governance and advances Africa’s representation in international decision-making.
According to Policy Brief-One issued by Office of the Prime Minister, Ethiopia secured one of four newly created seats during the 43rd Extraordinary Session of the ICAO Assembly in Montreal, Canada, following the expansion of the Council from 36 to 40 members.
The achievement reflects the convergence of Ethiopia’s eight-decade aviation legacy, sustained diplomatic engagement, African solidarity and South-South cooperation, positioning the country to contribute directly to shaping the future of international civil aviation.
A key factor behind Ethiopia’s election was its endorsement by the African Union as the continent’s sole candidate for the additional Council seat, with support from the African Civil Aviation Commission (AFCAC).
The endorsement represented a coordinated continental effort to strengthen Africa’s voice in global aviation institutions, positioning Ethiopia’s candidacy within a broader agenda of advancing the continent’s collective interests.
The diplomatic support also extended beyond Africa through the BRICS platform. The 18th BRICS Summit, held in New Delhi, explicitly welcomed Ethiopia’s candidacy in paragraph 105 of its New Delhi Declaration, recognizing the African Union’s endorsement of the country as the sole African candidate.
This wider recognition demonstrated how continental solidarity and cooperation among emerging economies can reinforce the participation of developing countries in international governance institutions.
Expanding Ethiopia’s Role in Global Aviation Governance
Ethiopia’s membership in the ICAO Council provides an important platform to participate directly in shaping international aviation policies and standards.
As the governing body responsible for overseeing ICAO’s work between Assembly sessions, the Council plays a central role in guiding international aviation cooperation and developing Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs) covering aviation safety, security, air navigation, environmental sustainability and technological innovation.
The position also gives Ethiopia an opportunity to contribute to global discussions on aviation decarbonization, carbon offsetting and sustainable aviation fuels, ensuring that emerging international regulations take into account the circumstances and development priorities of African countries and other developing aviation markets.
Office of the Prime Minister noted that the Council seat connects Ethiopia’s diplomatic engagement with its broader economic transformation ambitions.
With Ethiopian Airlines, expanding airport infrastructure, modernizing air navigation services and ICAO-aligned aviation training institutions, the country has an established aviation foundation upon which to build greater international connectivity and economic opportunities.
The Council membership is expected to further reinforce international confidence in Ethiopia’s aviation regulatory institutions, support the development of its aviation industry and strengthen Addis Ababa’s position as a major intercontinental passenger and cargo hub.
These opportunities have implications beyond the aviation sector, with improved connectivity potentially supporting export trade, tourism, foreign investment and the creation of skilled employment opportunities for Ethiopian professionals.
Advancing Africa’s Aviation Integration
Beyond its national significance, Ethiopia’s election provides an institutional platform to advance Africa’s shared aviation priorities within the global governance system.
Working in coordination with the African Union and AFCAC, Ethiopia is expected to champion initiatives aimed at accelerating the implementation of the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM), harmonizing regional airspace management, expanding intra-African connectivity and strengthening aviation safety and technical capacity across the continent.
These priorities are central to improving air transport links among African countries, facilitating trade and tourism, and supporting the continent’s broader economic integration agenda.
The development also comes at a time when Africa is seeking greater representation in international institutions and a stronger role in shaping global policies that directly affect its economic development.
The Office of the Prime Minister emphasized that maximizing the opportunities created by Ethiopia’s election requires sustained institutional readiness and coordinated engagement by aviation authorities, the private sector and young professionals.
It stressed the importance of translating diplomatic representation into institutional excellence, ensuring that the country’s new global mandate delivers tangible benefits for its aviation industry, citizens and the African continent.
Ethiopia’s election to the ICAO Council thus opens a new chapter in its aviation diplomacy, linking its longstanding aviation experience with greater participation in global decision-making and the advancement of Africa’s collective interests.

items.title: Le Premier ministre au domicile de la famille DAIKREO

original_payload.original_title: Le Premier ministre au domicile de la famille DAIKREO
original_payload.original_body:
C’est avec une profonde émotion et une compassion sincère que le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Amb. ALLAH MAYE Halina s’est rendu, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, au domicile de la famille du regretté CGP DAIKREO RAIWE KOLANDI, sis au quartier Moursal, dans le 6ᵉ arrondissement de la ville de N’Djaména, pour lui témoigner son soutien dans cette douloureuse épreuve.
Le Chef du Gouvernement est venu partager la peine d’une famille, d’une communauté et de toute une nation qui vient de perdre l’un de ses dignes fils.
Né le 1er janvier 1943 à Midaoré, dans le département du Mont Illi, province du Mayo-Kebbi Est, le patriarche DAIKREO s’est éteint le 19 novembre 2026 à N’Djaména, à l’âge de 83 ans, après une vie bien remplie, faite de sagesse, de labeur et de dévouement pour les siens.
Ses obsèques, empreintes de recueillement et de dignité, ont eu lieu ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, en présence de ses proches, parents, amis et connaissances venus nombreux lui rendre un dernier hommage.
Le défunt laisse derrière lui une immense famille éplorée : quatre épouses, 24 enfants, 74 petits-enfants et 16 arrière-petits-enfants, ainsi qu’un vide immense que nul ne saurait combler.
En s’inclinant devant la mémoire du disparu, le Premier ministre a présenté, au nom du Gouvernement et en son nom personnel, ses condoléances les plus attristées à la famille endeuillée. Il a imploré le Très-Haut d’accorder au défunt le repos éternel et de donner à sa famille la force et le courage nécessaires pour surmonter cette dure épreuve.
Après avoir présenté ses condoléances, le Chef du Gouvernement a signé le livre de condoléances ouvert en mémoire de l’illustre disparu.
Il était accompagné, pour la circonstance, du ministre de la Sécurité publique, Ali Ahmat Akhabache, et de quelques membres de son cabinet.

items.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row

original_payload.original_title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row
original_payload.original_body:
Uganda 's army said on Friday it planned to withdraw from a key  DR Congo  town and accused militias apparently allied to the Congolese government of stepping up attacks in the strife-torn eastern region.
The Ugandan announcement comes days after the DRC said it had summoned the Ugandan embassy's head of mission over remarks by the country's army chief.
The mineral-rich eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has been wracked by violence for more than 30 years, often drawing in its neighbours Uganda and  Rwanda  directly or through support for local armed groups.
UN Security Council demands Rwanda withdraw troops from eastern DR Congo
Ugandan armed forces (UPDF) have been deployed in Ituri and  North Kivu  provinceson the DRC's border with Uganda since 2021.
They were sent to back up the Congolese army against militants linked to the  Islamic State jihadist group.
The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), historically a Ugandan rebel coalition, was established in the eastern DRC in 1995 and regularly carries out killings in the deeply troubled region plagued by myriad armed groups.
The Congolese army is also fighting the armed FRN anti-governmental group, formerly known as  the M23 , which is backed by Rwanda, in the region.
Watch more  Predictable: DR Congo-Rwanda rivalry spills over to Francophonie summit
On Monday, Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of President  Yoweri Museveni , threatened on X to take control of the strategic Congolese town of Walikale in North Kivu province.
The FRN launched an offensive towards the town at the beginning of the month.
Kainerugaba – known for inflammatory posts on social media – had in a separate post also called for the unconditional surrender of the airport in Isiro, the provincial capital in Haut-Uele.
In response, Kinshasa announced the following day the summons of the Ugandan diplomat following what it called the "particularly serious" remarks.
The DRC "remains determined to ensure respect for its dignity and its institutions in the face of any form of provocation or interference", it said in a statement.
On Friday, the Ugandan army spokesman said on X that it would "soon" withdraw its forces from the town of Lubero in North Kivu which is close to a front line in fighting between Congolese and FRN forces.
Watch more  Uganda withdraws troops from peacekeeping mission in Somalia
In a separate post, the spokesman accused militia forces, including some apparently allied to the Congolese government, of stepping up attacks on civilians.
"These negative militia forces have increasingly mounted attacks against vulnerable communities, massacring women and children such as the Bahema and Tutsi communities in Ituri and the North Kivu region," he said.
"Under International Humanitarian Law (IHL), the UPDF retains the responsibility to extend protection to such vulnerable communities and will continue to do so whenever possible," he added.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)
original_payload.original_summary: Uganda's army on Friday said it planned to withdraw from the eastern DR Congo town of Lubero in North Kivu. The announcement came days after Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – son of President Yoweri Museveni – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, sparking a diplomatic spat between the two neighbouring nations.
original_payload.author: FRANCE 24

items.title: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners

original_payload.original_title: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners
original_payload.original_body:
Refugees  living in  South Africa  are being driven from their homes, businesses are being vandalised and foreigners are even being targeted in hospitals and universities. Behind this growing wave of  xenophobia  lies deep social anger, but also political rhetoric that blames  migrants  for the country's problems.
For those who once saw South Africa as a land of hope – an El Dorado – that era now seems firmly in the past.
original_payload.original_summary: South Africa was once a welcoming country; a refuge for those fleeing conflict and persecution. But for thousands of foreigners, the dream of a new life in South Africa is turning into more of a nightmare. Against a backdrop of unemployment and economic hardship, anti-immigration movements are gaining ground. Our correspondents report.
original_payload.author: Caroline DUMAY, Stefan CARSTENS, Eunice Masson

Single-layer vulnerability classifications obscure the dynamic, intersectional realities of the current crisis. Moving beyond status-based or geographic targeting to needs-based response requires anchoring interventions in actual socio-economic and demographic profiles derived from the latest assessments (MSNA, COD-PS, DTM, Rapid Gender Assessment, and specialized TWG consultations).
This document presents the outcomes of the Meaning-Making Workshop 2026, consolidating gender, age, and disability considerations and translating them into actionable recommendations for the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) 2027. The document was shared with and presented to the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), which brings together sector and cluster leads, in September 2026. It brings together the key materials and findings from the workshop, organized by the Gender in Humanitarian Action Working Group (GiHA WG) in collaboration with the Cross-Cutting Expertise Group—which includes the GiHA WG, Age and Disability Technical Working Group (TWG), Accountability to Affected People Working Group (AAP WG), and LGBTIQ+ Technical Working Group—as well as the Data Coordination Group, comprising REACH, IOM, and OCHA.

original_payload.original_title: Somalia: Radio Ergo Weekly Feedback Report, Issued: 27 Nov 2026
original_payload.original_body:
Somalia
Radio Ergo Weekly Feedback Report, Issued: 27 Nov 2026
Format
News and Press Release
Source
Radio Ergo
Posted
27 Nov 2026
Originally published
27 Nov 2026
Attachments
Download Report
(PDF | 386.24 KB)
Brief Summary
Commentary on rainfall and its positive impact on lives and livelihoods continued to form the bulk of the calls to Radio Ergo’s nationwide feedback platform in the week 19-25 November 2026. These calls came mostly from Jubbaland, South West, Hirshabelle, and some from Galmudug. However, some callers mainly in southern locations noted a tailing off of the rainfall, patchy areas without rain, and also intensely hot temperatures. A few in Gedo and Bay regions said they were now running short of water again. Drought conditions were cited in Bari. Several callers complained about influxes of mosquitoes and rising malaria cases, and wanted mosquito control measures. In Gedo region a number of IDP callers complained of hardships and their need for aid. The following summarises the calls by theme.
Health  – callers in Awdhegle in Lower Shabelle and Adado in Galgadud spoke of influxes of mosquitoes in their areas and a rise in malaria and wanted the menace to be brought under control. A caller in Gedo said the mosquitoes were causing illness with headaches and fever. A caller in Bardera said they had good rainfall, but mosquitoes were their main concern. A caller in Dollow also cited a mosquito influx, adding that despite the rain people were impoverished and aid agencies hadn’t visited the area for six months.
IDPs  – a caller in Iftin camp, Bardera, said they and their farms were doing well after the rain. On the other hand, a female caller in Bardera identifying as an IDP said they had received little rainfall, their crops had been attacked by pests and disease, and the schools had been shut for the past six months depriving the children of education. In Qurdubey, a caller called twice on behalf of displaced families who had lost their livestock. He said those families with a few livestock left were able to sell them for a living, but others like them were facing hardship and challenging conditions including poor sanitation. He added an appeal for aid.
Aid  – a caller in Dollow complained that they had been registered by aid groups a few days ago, but had not received the cash aid they thought they were going to get. Another caller, location unspecified, wanted a resumption of the cash aid they used to get from WFP that had stopped.
Food Security  – a caller in Bardera said he wanted to share information about the high inflation and rising costs of basics they were facing.
Locusts –  a caller in Kismayo said he had a farm near the airport and was concerned about locusts. He wanted to know how the farmers could protect their crops.
Climate  – a caller in Baidoa, Bay region, said they’d been experiencing intense heat and wanted to know if this was because of climate change. Similarly, a caller in Bahdo, Galgadud, said recent days had been intensely hot and people wondered if it was a sign of rain to come, or of climate change. Other callers in Guriel, Dollow, and Kismayo also described intense heat in their areas.
Agriculture  – farmers in southern and some central areas complained of pests damaging a range of produce including potatoes, beans, sesame, sorghum, maize, lettuce and tomatoes. They wanted to talk with experts on Radio Ergo’s weekly farming programme.
Livestock  – a caller in Bardera said his camels had  dukan  (trypanosomiasis) and the medicine he was injecting them with was not working. He wanted veterinary advice. Several herders in Jubbaland complained of foot and mouth affecting their herds. A caller in Beletweyne wanted to know more about how pre-export livestock inspections and certifications were processed in Somalia.
Drought & water shortage  – a caller in Rako-raho, Bari region, said they faced drought in the area and that many people had already migrated away. He added that they were in a desperate situation and needed the Puntland authority to reach them with aid. One caller in Dusamareb said they faced drought and conflict. Several in Bay region said the rain had been poor or had stopped already, with one describing the drying up of crops and grazing. A caller in Bardera said rainfall had been little and their farms were failing due to water shortages. A female caller said that odder and water shortage were affecting their livestock. Another female caller in Lower Juba said they weren’t having rainfall, the heat was intense, and their livestock were struggling.
Rainfall  – a female caller in Farjeni, Bari, said they had received some light rain. A caller in Harardhere, Mudug, said they were getting heavy rain and doing well. In Galgadud, callers spoke of decent rain in Bahdo, Guriel, Abudwak, and Adado, with several noting intense heat. In Hiran, callers in Buleburte, Af-ad, and El-gal noted good rain and conditions for their livestock and farms. Callers in Baidoa, Burhakaba, and Dinsor in Bay region cited beneficial rain.
